articles.title: Independent regulator report says English football finances are 'dangerously exposed'
articles.summary: English football's finances are "dangerously exposed, with the majority of clubs living on the edge of financial disaster", a new report says.
articles.body:
English football's finances are "dangerously exposed, with the majority of clubs living on the edge of financial disaster", according to a landmark report by the independent football regulator.

Research by the watchdog found 94% of clubs are loss-making, and more than 60% of EFL and National League clubs are technically insolvent.

The regulator (IFR) warns of "a dangerous cocktail of rising debt and an over-reliance on owner funding, leaving clubs and their fans at risk".

The 'State of the Game' report also suggests that despite the economic success of the Premier League, the financial 'cliff-edges' between and within leagues have grown significantly.

94% of clubs in the top five English leagues made losses in 2025-26

17 clubs across the EFL and National League would be loss-making even if their players played for free

66% of clubs could not survive for more than 90 days without new owner funding

29% of clubs reported they could not survive more than 30 days without such funding

68% of clubs have no contingency plan if their owner walks away

The IFR claims "the underlying foundations of the pyramid are under intense strain and require urgent reform", and its report "should serve as a wake-up call" for English football.

"Seventeen clubs are now trading in such a way that if their players played for free, their non-playing costs would mean they would go bust," IFR chair David Kogan told BBC Sport.

"Thirty-two clubs are operating on only 30 days' cash. If the owner chooses not to pay cash at the end of the month, those clubs go bust.

"That is a very, very risky scenario. This is the moment of addressing these problems before money starts to dry up.

"We can actually fix the house while the sun is still shining and that's essentially what our role is going to be in this."

Regulator would quit over Man City interference

Tasked with improving teams' financial sustainability, the IFR outlined six areas of concern around financial risk, and urged clubs to put robust contingency plans in place in case owner funding is withdrawn.

Despite years of talks, the Premier League and EFL are yet to agree a new funding settlement that would see the top flight share more money with the rest of the pyramid.

The IFR has the power to impose a deal and warns that "if football can't find a solution we will consider our next steps and will not hesitate to use all the powers at our disposal to bring about lasting change".

It also urges action on rising losses and calls on clubs to show how they take fans' views into account, and the steps they are taking to improve boardroom diversity and governance.

The average Premier League club now earns more than eight times the average Championship side

The existing system of parachute payments paid by the Premier League to Championship clubs who have been relegated "contributes to the incentives for Championship clubs to overspend which drives up player wage inflation"

Net transfer debt is going up and deferred transfer payments and transfer financing create links between clubs, owners and lenders which increases "the potential for financial stress to spread across the game".

"Nobody in football for 100 years has believed that football was trading in a solvent and effective state," Kogan said.

"It's not how football has ever really operated.

"But I think now where there's so much more money involved, the extremes get more extreme.

"We knew the problems were there, I don't think anybody realised that the data was going to show quite how dramatic they are."

The Premier League, the EFL, the Football Association and the Football Supporters' Association have all issued statements welcoming the findings.

BBC Sport outlines some of the key points in the report.

Clubs increasingly mortgaging off future transfer cash

Over the past five years there has been a growing trend to effectively mortgage off instalments a club is due to receive in transfer payments in return for an immediate injection of cash.

Called 'transfer financing', it has become "an increasingly important source of liquidity".

In 2020-21, transfer financing stood at £55m. By 2024-25 it had reached £779m - a more than 14-fold increase.

Now about £1.2bn of future transfer income has already been monetised through financing arrangements - an almost 22-fold rise on 2020-21.

Across English football, payments for transfer outgoings are about 3.3 times transfer incomings.

In 2025-26, English clubs reported approximately £4.8bn in transfer payables but only £1.5bn in transfer receivables - a net transfer debt of about £3.3bn.

The EFL's deteriorating financial outlook

The report says the financial situation is worsening for clubs across the EFL and National League.

Most Championship, League One and League Two clubs hold less than 30 days of cash.

More than 60% of EFL and National League clubs have liabilities exceeding the book value of their assets.

Twenty clubs - primarily in the Championship, League One and National League -spent more than 80% of revenue on player wages.

The majority of League One clubs spend more than 40% of revenue on player wages, including two spending more than 100%.

Wage costs have increased across all leagues between 2021-22 and 2025-26:

Seventeen of 18 (94%) EFL club owners surveyed were in favour of more robust cost controls - as one investor told the report: "the single biggest issue is player wages".

Average League One losses increased from 6% of revenue in 1992-93 to almost 50% in 2024-25. In League Two, it stands at 40%.

Many clubs rely on owner funding on a just-in-time basis, receiving frequent injections throughout the year.

The majority of EFL and National League clubs do not have a contingency plan if their owner becomes unable or unwilling to continue financing operations.

This leaves them particularly exposed given their limited access to alternative sources of finance.

"League One and the League Two clubs will receive significantly more funding [through a new deal with the Premier League]," Kogan said.

"That funding will be used along with a development fund and a liquidity fund potentially to help them get over the humps they're all currently facing."

In respect of both liquidity and solvency, the report says many football clubs "would not currently meet the requirement under the Football Governance Act to hold 'appropriate financial resources'."

Clubs are required to meet this standard by May 2030.

"Owners are very well aware of the need now for some sort of coherent structure in which costs are being managed," Kogan said.

Kogan added that the new financial distribution deal between the Premier League and the EFL is close.

Gap between the Premier League and the rest

It will not be news that the gap between the Premier League and the Championship has grown.

In 1992-93, the average Premier League club earned £10.5m, which was 2.7 times the £3.9m earned by the average Championship club.

By 2024-25 it was £341m, or 8.7 times the £38.9m in the second tier.

The revenue gap within the Championship has also grown, partly because of the increase in the size of parachute payments.

From 2007-08 to 2025-26, the amount a non-parachute Championship club received in solidarity payments from the Premier League increased from £0.9m to £5.3m.

But a year-one parachute club saw payments increase from £12m to £48.7m.

The absolute revenue gap between the big six and the rest of the Premier League has widened significantly, too.

In 1992-93, the six biggest clubs in terms of revenue earned £9.4m more on average. By 2024-25, this average revenue gap had grown to £421m.

The big six account for 56% Premier League revenues, with 44% split between the remaining 14 teams.

articles.title: Man City charges: Football regulator will quit if independence compromised
articles.summary: The head of English football's independent regulator says he will resign if he encounters any political interference over Manchester City's future.
articles.body:
The head of English football's independent regulator says he will resign if he encounters any political interference over the future of Manchester City .

As chairman of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR), David Kogan has the power to assess the suitability of club owners and executives.

If an independent commission's findings that the club broke Premier League financial rules are upheld, the watchdog could even force a sale.

Last month, the Prime Minister Andy Burnham was criticised for saying he would be "really concerned" if the scandal led to Manchester City 's Abu Dhabi owners selling the club.

"They've been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester and obviously the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is," he added.

When asked about Burnham's comments, Kogan told BBC Sport: "The Prime Minister is entirely entitled to make his own observations on anything.

"We are independent. That is in the name. I am the chairman of the Independent Football Regulator and independence absolutely runs through everything we're doing.

"And no politician has tried to influence and would try to influence anything we do on that."

When asked what he would do if he did come under political pressure over the case, Kogan replied: "I would resign."

An independent commission found City had broken rules over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018. Owners Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) - a private investment company belonging to United Arab Emirates vice-president and deputy prime minister Sheikh Mansour - are said to have topped up the value of commercial deals as part of a "disguised funding scheme" to the scale of £830m.

City insist they are innocent and have appealed.

How much did Man City's rule breaking cost your team?

'Criticised for what?' - Maresca defends celebrations

The prime minister initially told the BBC of his concerns, before later denying his reaction had "downplayed the seriousness of the findings".

However, some Premier League clubs were so "astonished" by Burnham's stance that sources told BBC Sport they were "concerned" about political interference in the appeal process.

Burnham's previous role as mayor of Greater Manchester has led to questions about his relationship with City's Abu Dhabi ownership.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch demanded all details of meetings between the prime minister and senior figures at the club are released. The government released these details on Monday .

Speaking at the launch of the IFR's State of the Game report, Kogan said, "As far as we, as the regulator, are concerned, we have a very clear course of action that is governed by statute and we are going to follow that course of action, and no comment by any politician or indeed any individual is going to affect what we do".

Kogan's hiring as IFR chair was the subject of an inquiry by the Commissioner for Public Appointments over his historic links to the Labour Party, having contributed money to the leadership campaigns of former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer and culture secretary Lisa Nandy.

Shadow Culture Minister Louie French has written to the government, citing "concerns about the IFR's ability to adjudicate this case fairly, free from political interference".

In response, Kogan said: "I can tell you absolutely categorically that any politician who's trying to meddle in this for political purposes is welcome to try and welcome to do it, but I am going to stand by the probity of the organisation that I lead. If anybody wishes to challenge those after we've acted, that's entirely up to them."

The independent panel will hold a sanctions hearing - which could take months to convene - to decide on City's punishment.

The club can appeal both the guilty verdicts and the sanction, leaving the league in a state of uncertainty.

City's punishment could range from a huge fine, being deducted points or being ejected from the Premier League.

Asked how crucial it is that it was resolved as soon as possible, Kogan said: "I think it's very important."

Kogan added that the case was "raising very serious issues if Manchester City on appeal is found to be guilty of the allegations within those findings".

"We are waiting like everybody else to see what the independent panel will do… and then we will bring in a view in terms of our own investigation and statutory powers if we need to do so.

"Our powers relate to individual owners, directors and senior executives. They refer to whether people are in a position to run a club in a way that is safe, coherent and done with probity, and we will be examining those things."

When asked if the IFR could withhold a club license from City when it starts awarding them from next month, Kogan said: "I'm not going to begin to comment on any actions we may take until we've had a chance to assess it."

And on whether the case had raise questions about the state-connected ownership of clubs, Kogan replied: "No, I don't think specifically it does. We have no powers to prevent state ownership of clubs. It's not within our remit. But I don't think you can apply a general observation about type of ownership to one particular example."

An independent commission held a 42-day hearing in 2024 that led to the verdict announced last month, with City also guilty of all charges except one relating to non-cooperation with the Premier League investigation.

The commission's report said that "a number of important club witnesses gave false evidence in key respects and that some knowingly gave untrue and dishonest evidence".

articles.title: Otro escándalo de Infantino: habría ocultado un sobresueldo de más de un millón y medio de euros
articles.standfirst: The Times destapa un sobresueldo con el que habría llevado una vida de lujo en Miami
articles.summary: The Times destapa un sobresueldo con el que habría llevado una vida de lujo en Miami
articles.body: Según se acerca la fecha de las elecciones en FIFA, a Gianni Infantino se le acelera la publicación de noticias negativas sobre su figura como presidente del fútbol mundial. A sus problemas con la oficina que alquiló por casi 4 millones de dólares durante más de siete años y que permaneció casi vacía en una torre Trump se une ahora la aparición de un informe de The Times sobre un supuesto sobresueldo, no declarado, que le habría permitido llevar una vida de lujo en Miami. La información de The Times asegura que "FIFA pagó millones de dólares a Gianni Infantino además de su sueldo habitual y sus primas, pero no declaró públicamente dichos pagos, lo que supone una presunta infracción de sus propios estatutos". Ese sobresueldo, de 1,76 millones de dólares (1,57 millones de euros) estaría pagado por la empresa organizadora del Mundial en Estados Unidos, FWC2026 US Inc, y habría sido detectado por la declaración fiscal presentada ante el Servicio de Impuestos Internos de Estados Unidos por la propia empresa. En 2024, FIFA pagó un salario a Infantino de casi 4,6 millones de euros, un sueldo que, según The Times, debe ser parecido al que cobró en los años 2025 y 2026. Miguel Maduro, expresidente del Comité de Gobernanza de la FIFA, declaró a The Times: "Se trata de una clara infracción de las normas si recibe otros pagos de empresas vinculadas a la FIFA y esto no se hace público. Los estatutos de la FIFA imponen una obligación de total transparencia". La información del diario británico incide en la vida lujosa que el presidente de FIFA llevaría en Miami, donde reside desde 2022. Hasta entonces vivía en Qatar, pero una vez terminó el Mundial disputado allí puso rumbo a Florida. "Fuentes del mundo del fútbol internacional han cuestionado si este dinero se destinó a sufragar el uso de la mansión frente al mar situada en una de las zonas más codiciadas de Miami Beach; la FIFA no ha confirmado si este fue el caso", dice The Times. En un comunicado de FIFA que publica el Telegraph este martes, el organismo que regula el fútbol mundial niega las acusaciones: "La FIFA no paga un segundo sueldo al presidente de la FIFA y cumple con todos los requisitos de información relativos a la remuneración. La remuneración anual del presidente de la FIFA, así como otras prestaciones contractuales, las decide el subcomité independiente de remuneraciones La FIFA rechaza enérgicamente cualquier acusación de que haya omitido revelar información financiera y de que haya infringido los estatutos de la FIFA. Las cuentas de la FIFA son auditadas de forma independiente, y todas las declaraciones se ajustan a la normativa fiscal de Suiza, Estados Unidos y otros países".

articles.title: El escudo ya corona la fachada del Bernabéu
articles.standfirst: El emblema madridista luce delante de la palabra ‘Bernabéu’ separado por una barra vertical
articles.summary: El emblema madridista luce delante de la palabra ‘Bernabéu’ separado por una barra vertical
articles.body: El rótulo del Santiago Bernabéu ya está completo. Tal y como informó MARCA hace días, el Real Madrid planeaba rematarlo esta semana, y así ha sido. Este martes 13 de octubre, durante la mañana, el club instaló el escudo en la fachada del estadio, junto a las letras que deletrean el nombre del coliseo. El emblema quedó situado delante de la palabra ‘Bernabéu’, de la que lo separa una barra vertical, en un conjunto que remata la imagen exterior del recinto. El origen de todo se remonta al pasado 15 de agosto, cuando el club colocó las letras de ‘Bernabéu’ en la fachada de cara al estreno liguero en casa. Aquella instalación, sin embargo, se quedó corta: ni el escudo del Real Madrid ni el logotipo de la marca comercial del estadio llegaron a montarse entonces. El rótulo lucía el nombre del recinto, pero sin el emblema que lo identifica y sin la denominación completa de Santiago Bernabéu. El resultado no dejó satisfecha a buena parte de la afición, que echó en falta tanto el distintivo del club como el nombre íntegro del estadio. La imagen de la fachada, incompleta, provocó cierta decepción entre los seguidores madridistas, que esperaban ver reflejada en la coraza del nuevo Bernabéu la identidad del club con todos sus símbolos. Esa reclamación tiene ya respuesta. Durante los días previos, los operarios habían trabajado sobre la fachada para preparar la estructura que sostiene el emblema, a la altura donde están situadas las letras, antes de culminar la instalación en la jornada de este martes. Con este paso, el estadio da por cerrada una de las últimas asignaturas pendientes de su renovación en lo que a imagen exterior se refiere.

articles.title: El Real Madrid renueva su alianza de moda con Louis Vuitton
articles.standfirst: La Maison francesa renueva su línea ‘Formal Wear’ y ‘Formal Travel’ para los equipos masculino y femenino de fútbol y el masculino de baloncesto
articles.summary: La Maison francesa renueva su línea ‘Formal Wear’ y ‘Formal Travel’ para los equipos masculino y femenino de fútbol y el masculino de baloncesto
articles.body: Louis Vuitton ha presentado este martes 13 de octubre la nueva colección de su colaboración con el Real Madrid, coincidiendo con el arranque de la temporada 2026/27 de la Liga de Campeones para el equipo masculino de fútbol. Se trata del segundo año de una alianza que la firma francesa amplía ahora, por primera vez, a los equipos masculino y femenino de fútbol y al masculino de baloncesto. Las líneas ‘Formal Wear’ y ‘Formal Travel’, diseñadas específicamente para los jugadores y representantes del club, han sido concebidas por el estudio masculino de Louis Vuitton bajo la dirección creativa de Pharrell Williams. La propuesta, inspirada en la colección ‘Louis Vuitton Trunk’ lanzada en febrero de 2026, combina nuevas incorporaciones con diseños ya existentes. Entre las novedades del apartado ‘Formal Travel’ figura una chaqueta reversible de nailon con el Monogram completo en el interior, el escudo del Real Madrid bordado en la parte delantera y una etiqueta interior personalizada con las firmas de ambas entidades. La colección suma también un jersey azul marino con el escudo bordado en la espalda, un polo beige que sustituye al anterior azul marino, un cinturón reversible y una nueva gorra azul marino. El ‘Formal Wear’, por su parte, mantiene el traje de la pasada temporada, ahora acompañado de una nueva camisa azul de finas rayas blancas y el citado polo beige. El conjunto se completa con un abrigo de cachemira de la colección permanente de la Maison, dotado de una bufanda extraíble de Monogram, el escudo del club bordado y las iniciales de cada jugador en la etiqueta interior. La marroquinería, además, se suma a la celebración del 130 aniversario del Monogram a través de la línea ‘Mon Monogram’. Las colecciones ‘Formal Wear’ y ‘Formal Travel’ de Louis Vuitton para el Real Madrid no están a la venta, al tratarse de prendas exclusivas para el club. No obstante, algunos de los modelos emblemáticos de la firma en los que se inspiran estas piezas, así como el servicio de personalización ‘Mon Monogram’, sí pueden adquirirse en tiendas y en la web de la Maison.

articles.title: Villarreal - Nápoles | Resumen, resultado y goles del partido de Champions League
articles.summary: Aquí toda la historia de Gerard Moreno: ingresa en el club de los cinco del Villarreal Precisamente Gerard Moreno sigue haciendo historia en amarillo.
articles.body:
Última hora del Villarreal - Nápoles en directo:

El Villarreal disputa esta noche un partido marcado en rojo en el calendario de la presente temporada. Y es que la experiencia de la pasada edición en Liga de Campeones ha enseñado a los amarillo que, con este nuevo formato, no se pueden dejar pasar oportunidades y que los trenes no esperan. Si bien es cierto que el Nápoles llega como un rival importante al estadio de La Cerámica, los próximos rivales (Liverpool en Anfield y PSG en Vila-real) no invitan a esperar más tiempo antes de lograr una victoria que evite abrir las puertas a los fantasmas de la última campaña.

El partido llega con pocas horas de descanso tras un partido especialmente intenso en lo físico y en lo anímico como el que los azulejeros vivieron este pasado sábado en el estadio Santiago Bernabéu. Un desgaste que puede pasar factura , ya que la intención de Iñigo es que repitan gran parte de los futbolistas que formaron parte del once en el coliseo blanco. Es por ello que el navarro ha apelado a la ilusión por lograr la primera victoria continental de la temporada como mejor antídoto contra el cansancio.

Tras un complicado inicio de temporada , donde la falta de victorias generó dudas en un entorno acostumbrado a ganar (cierto es que en Liga y no en Europa durante la pasada temporada), los castellonenses calmaron las aguas con dos victorias sanadoras antes del parón. Ante el Real Madrid los azulejeros sufrieron una derrota previsible , si bien es cierto que dieron la cara y demostraron haber encontrado la fiabilidad necesaria para poder competir en escenarios como el que se van a encontrar esta noche, donde la presión ya comienza a jugar su papel.

Una parte importante en la recuperación de los amarillos llegó gracias al cambio de sistema por el que apostó el técnico antes del parón. Con Moleiro como 10 y con dos hombres abiertos a banda por detrás un referente ofensivo. Las bajas de Buchanan y Pépé (este último por problemas oculares) para las próximas semanas, complican dicha opción, por lo que el navarro deberá buscar alternativas dentro de la plantilla.

El regreso de Saliba al once, tras ser involuntario protagonista en el Bernabéu en la expulsión de Vinicius, y la opción de Carlos Romero adelantando su posición para jugar como centrocampista, es una de las alternativas que baraja el técnico. La otra es repetir un trivote como el que presentó ante lo blando o en la primera jornada europea ante el Borussia de Dortmund. La entrada de Mikautadze , necesitado de un gran partido esta temporada, apunta a ser la otra gran novedad.

Un Nápoles al alza y la espina de Allegri

Tras firmar, como lo amarillos, un inicio irregular, el Nápoles llega reforzado tras su contundente victoria este pasado fin de semana. La victoria por 3-0 ante el Frosinone supuso un paso al frente para los de Massimiliano Allegri. Además Kevin De Bruyne firmó un doblete para demostrar que su fútbol sigue vigente.

Todavía con bajas significativas los partenopeos recuperaron este pasado fin de semana al escocés McTominay . Recuperado de sus problemas cardiovasculares, será titular esta noche en La Cerámica.

Allegri ensayó un inédito 3-4-3 por primera vez esta temporada. Una fórmula que podría repetir en Vila-real sin descartar un regreso a una línea de cuatro defensas. En cualquiera de ambas formaciones parte un ex amarillo como es Rafa Marín.

El técnico italiano regresa a Vila-real con la espina que le queda tras su último duelo ante los amarillos en el que, como técnico de la Juve, fue apeado de forma contundente en los octavos de final de la Liga de Campeones 21/22 a manos del equipo entrenado por Unai Emery. Tras empatar a uno en Vila-real, en Italia los amarillos golearon por un contundente 0-3, lo que provocó grande críticas hacia el técnico de Livorno.

El Villarreal ha enderezado el rumbo y, pese a la derrota en el Bernabéu, es un equipo que está creciendo y empezando a parecerse lo que a lo que se esperaba de él. Esa confianza que empieza a tener en su juego y el apoyo de la grada debería llevarle a sumar su primera victoria en la fase Liga de la Champions.

articles.title: Peter Gulacsi sufre un robo a mano armada en su casa con él y su familia dentro
articles.standfirst: El meta húngaro es baja para el duelo de Champions ante el Nápoles
articles.summary: El meta húngaro es baja para el duelo de Champions ante el Nápoles
articles.body: El guardameta del Villarreal, Peter Gulacsi, será baja esta noche en el partido que su equipo va a disputar en La Cerámica ante el Nápoles a causa del fuerte impacto emocional sufrido tras el robo a mano armada del que ha sido víctima en las últimas horas. Tal y como el club de La Plana ha informado, el futbolista sufrió un robo a mano armada durante esta pasada madrugada mientras se encontraba con su familia en su domicilio. La entidad amarilla ha informado que, afortunadamente, ningún integrante de su familia ha resultado herido. El golpe emocional ha sido tal que el jugador no está en condiciones de disputar un partido como el que esta noche disputan los amarillos ante el Nápoles Peter Gulacsi, que llegó este verano al Villarreal, vive con su esposa y sus dos hijos pequeños, lo que da buena cuenta del impacto que para la familia ha supuesto el susto sufrido. No es la primera vez que ocurre un hecho similar con un futbolista del equipo amarillo. Temporadas atrás jugadores como Toko Ekambi o Zambo Anguissa ya sufrieron situaciones similares. También en el Valencia , en anteriores campañas, han sido varios los futbolistas que denunciaban estos hechos, como por ejemplo Garay, Gabriel Paulista o Kondogbia.

articles.title: 'Burn the F--king Boats,' UCLA HC Bob Chesney's Intense Speech Before Oregon Upset Shown in Video
articles.summary: UCLA football head coach Bob Chesney gave a fiery and intense speech in the Autzen Stadium tunnel prior to the Bruins taking the field and beating host Oregon 17-15 last Saturday.
articles.body:
UCLA football head coach Bob Chesney gave a fiery and intense speech in the Autzen Stadium tunnel prior to the Bruins taking the field and beating host Oregon 17-15 last Saturday.

The No. 12 Bruins are enjoying an incredible resurgence under Chesney, the former James Madison head coach who led the Dukes to the College Football Playoff last season.

This one may have been a bit personal for Chesney, as JMU lost 51-34 at Oregon in the first round of the CFP.

This year was different. UCLA outplayed Oregon, taking a 17-6 lead before holding on for the two-point win. The Ducks committed seven turnovers (two interceptions, five fumbles), and UCLA running back Wayne Knight rushed for 103 yards and a touchdown.

UCLA will look to move to 6-0 (4-0 in Big Ten) on Saturday evening when the Bruins host Wisconsin at 7:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Florian Wirtz: Should Liverpool drop Germany playmaker?
articles.summary: More than a year since his £116m move, Florian Wirtz is still struggling to hit top form at Liverpool - so does he need to be dropped?
articles.body:
At the end of the 2024-25 season, Liverpool head coach Arne Slot flew to the south of France to honour talks with Rayan Cherki.

Cherki was on Liverpool 's shortlist in their hunt for an attacking midfielder but the main target was Florian Wirtz - who was also wanted by Bayern Munich and Manchester City .

Once Wirtz said his preference was to move to Anfield and join the then-Premier League champions, the £116m deal became a formality.

At the time, his arrival felt like a quality acquisition for Liverpool , but more than a year on things are still not clicking.

The German has scored seven goals and provided 11 assists over 56 Reds appearances, but had no goal involvements against any of the top-10 teams in the Premier League last season.

This term, Wirtz has started every game in the league and Champions League so far - managing just one assist across seven matches.

Those struggles were summed up on Sunday against Manchester City when new Reds boss Andoni Iraola - who succeeded Slot in the summer - replaced Wirtz with Trey Nyoni in the 66th minute, shortly after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off and Erling Haaland broke the deadlock.

Wirtz is only 23 but so is Cherki, who put the icing on the cake in City's 3-0 win at Anfield with an exquisite goal - the kind we have become used to seeing since his £30m move from Lyon in June 2025.

Cherki cost less than a third of what Liverpool paid for Wirtz, but has already scored 16 goals and provided 18 assists in 65 City appearances.

The France attacker has also shown an ability to provide crucial game-changing moments. Liverpool fans haven't seen anywhere near enough of that from Wirtz yet.

"Wirtz has so much ability. I wish I had that ability because he just glides. He makes it look effortless - but he doesn't hurt teams," former Liverpool defender Steven Warnock told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"He doesn't impact the game enough. He drifts in and out of games. He's here for 10 or 20 seconds and then he disappears for five or 10 minutes and you think where is he now?"

After Liverpool 's defeat by Man City, Jamie Carragher said it was time for Iraola to drop Wirtz.

"I think he needs to come out of the team, I said that last time out and I'm going to say it again," Carragher told Sky Sports.

" Liverpool played well [against Man City] for a lot of the game before the Gravenberch red card but they didn't create a chance, so they have a real problem with scoring goals and creating chances and that's what you got Wirtz for.

"He's not giving you anything defensively and he's not giving you anything going the other way. I don't want anyone to pile in on the lad but I think we're justified in saying we need more and we can't wait."

'Anyone who loves football can see Wirtz is outstanding'

Given that Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai are all currently sidelined, it would be a big call to drop Wirtz - but Liverpool have two games every week between now and the November international break.

With Gravenberch suspended for Saturday's trip to Brentford , Iraola will likely keep the Dutch midfielder in for Wednesday's Champions League game against LASK in Austria and give a start to Nyoni. More changes are expected from Sunday's defeat.

When it comes to the intensity of the top flight, Wirtz is still finding his feet, but his best performance this season came in the Champions League against Atletico Madrid and he was unlucky not to get an assist when Bradley Barcola fired wide.

Asked on Tuesday if Wirtz needed more time, Iraola defended his player and said: "The other day, he probably he didn't have his best game but he has had good games with us this season.

"Everyone starts looking for answers. He had some good performances in the national team - he scored one goal and he will have better or worse games.

"But I would like to look at it more collectively and more how they help us play and get results and after that I don't care who scores. I think it's a more collective thing."

Seeing Wirtz excel for Germany under Jurgen Klopp is proof - if it was needed - as to why he was seen as one of the hottest talents in world football when he joined Liverpool .

"Attacking players always need a functioning team that works well around them. Anyone who loves football can still see how outstanding Florian is as a player," Klopp said recently.

That is also a view shared by Steven Gerrard.

"I can just picture him beating himself up on how his Liverpool thing has started. This kid is a major talent in my opinion. I've seen enough to believe and give him a chance. I think he needs help and support now," Gerrard told The Overlap.

Wirtz created 95 chances from open play in all competitions last season - at least 27 more than any other Liverpool player - and his fizzing pass for Victor Munoz's equaliser against Nottingham Forest in August showed a glimpse of his class, but those moments have been few and far in between.

Against City at the weekend there was a moment at 0-0 when Wirtz hit an effort wide despite having Barcola and Milos Kerkez in space on his left. It was a poor decision from a man desperate for a big moment.

Back in August, Wirtz spoke candidly about how he felt "more ready" for his second season at Anfield. The physicality was a key aspect, with bulking up a big focus of his first campaign.

"I definitely learned a lot. I just learned how Premier League football is played and I think I am more ready for my second season because I know how it is now. I am really excited for my next season," Wirtz said then.

He impressed in pre-season but two months into the new campaign, Wirtz needs to start delivering sooner rather than later.

If not, then Iraola will be left with a tough decision to make.

articles.title: El Alba acumula récords negativos
articles.standfirst: No encajaba un 5-0 desde 2004 y su inicio liguero es el peor en Segunda desde... ¡el año 1940!
articles.summary: No encajaba un 5-0 desde 2004 y su inicio liguero es el peor en Segunda desde... ¡el año 1940!
articles.body: El Albacete sufrió el lunes en el José Zorrilla una dolorosa derrota ante el Real Valladolid en el estreno de Joseba Etxeberria en el banquillo albacetista. Una goleada que el equipo manchego no encajaba desde hacía más de 22 años: la última se remonta al 1 de febrero de 2004, cuando fue el Barça quien le infringió tamaño castigo...en Primera división. Con esta derrota, el Alba sigue colista con un solo punto de 27 posibles tras nueve jornadas, con un empate y ocho derrotas, cuatro de ellas de forma consecutiva. Un inicio liguero que solo iguala en cuanto a lo negativo, el conjunto del EHA de Tánger en 1940, según dato aportado por la cuenta de X LaLigaEnDirecto. El golpe también tuvo su reflejo fuera del terreno de juego. Varias decenas de aficionados decidieron escenificar su hartazgo con una concentración de protesta en la Ciudad Deportiva con el objetivo de mostrar su descontento a la expedición que volvía de Valladolid. El próximo compromiso será el sábado en Gijón, en El Molinón 'Enrique Castro Quini' y se van acabando los argumentos para quien haya elegido creer. Etxeberria se refirió a esa cita como una oportunidad para reaccionar, una más: el técnico vasco quiere "enfocarlo como una oportunidad de poder conseguir la victoria y a partir de ahí crecer". El Alba necesita esa victoria para empezar a creer. Necesita de forma imperiosa buenas noticias y dejar de coleccionar récords negativos.

articles.title: Bournemouth open to Alex Scott sale in January
articles.summary: Bournemouth are open to selling England midfielder Alex Scott in January under certain conditions.
articles.body:
Bournemouth are open to selling England midfielder Alex Scott in January under certain conditions.

The 23-year-old has been pushing to leave Vitality Stadium since rejecting two contract offers at the end of last season, but Bournemouth insisted he was not for sale throughout the recent international break.

However, after a final round of talks with his representatives, senior sources say the Cherries are willing to sanction Scott's sale if an offer of about £100m arrives in January.

Another condition will be Bournemouth 's position in the Premier League table. If they are struggling towards the bottom of the league then the club may decide they need Scott to help secure survival.

It remains a significant shift in stance after a summer in which Bournemouth rejected interest from a host of clubs - with every member of the Premier League's so-called "big six" believed to have made contact to varying degrees.

All clubs were told not to make an offer or approach the player, although Chelsea tested the water with an initial £60m bid rising to £64m in add-ons which was rejected.

Chelsea and Liverpool are believed to retain an interest, with Manchester City , Manchester United and Tottenham having moved on to other targets over the summer.

Liverpool would be in a strong position, with manager Andoni Iraola maintaining close relationships with his former club, both with Scott himself and figures in Bournemouth 's leadership.

Meanwhile, Chelsea have previously had encouragement from Scott's representatives to pursue a deal.

Scott is currently out for at least a month with a thigh injury sustained during England's 7-0 win over Croatia in the Nations League.

He remains on the same contract he signed when joining Bournemouth from Bristol City in 2023 for a fee of £25m, which expires in 2028.

Bitter-sweet decision for Cherries - analysis

The decision to consider Scott's sale is a bitter-sweet one for Bournemouth .

The club entered the season insisting none of their prized assets, including Scott, Rayan and Eli Junior Kroupi, would be sold before the summer of 2027.

However, they have since reluctantly concluded they would be prepared to let Scott leave if their valuation is met.

Bournemouth can point to a market in which spending on midfielders has reached unprecedented levels across the Premier League.

Three players have commanded fees of more than £100m in the position and the Cherries are seeking a similar amount for Scott.

A TransferRoom report, released on Tuesday, shows spending on defensive midfielders rose by "191% to 1.38bn euros , while the average fee increased by 156% to 9.9m euros - the highest average fee of any position."

There is also frustration within the club that Scott picked up an injury while away with England.

He entered the camp carrying tightness, only for the issue to worsen and leave him sidelined for about six weeks.

That came after Kroupi sustained a serious injury in pre-season, causing him to miss the entire season so far, with a return not expected until November.

New manager Marco Rose is yet to win a league match, with the 5-1 defeat by Chelsea representing the lowest point of his tenure so far.

There remains hope results will improve. Iraola endured an even longer winless run when he first took charge, while there is excitement surrounding Bournemouth 's Europa League campaign.

Their European adventure began with an impressive win against Real Sociedad and continues with a home game against Sturm Graz on Thursday.

articles.title: La radiografía que alarma al fútbol inglés: el 94% de los clubes pierde dinero y podrían correr peligro
articles.standfirst: El regulador independiente alerta de una pirámide "peligrosamente expuesta", con más del 60% de los clubes de EFL y National League técnicamente insolventes: las claves del informe del que se hace eco 'BBC'
articles.summary: El regulador independiente alerta de una pirámide "peligrosamente expuesta", con más del 60% de los clubes de EFL y National League técnicamente insolventes: las claves del informe del que se hace eco 'BBC'
articles.body: Las cuentas del fútbol inglés han encendido todas las alarmas. El 94% de los clubes de las cinco principales ligas registró pérdidas durante la temporada 2025-26 y más del 60% de los equipos de la EFL y la National League son técnicamente insolventes. Es la fotografía que deja el informe 'Estado del juego' elaborado por el organismo regulador independiente del fútbol, la IFR, que describe unas finanzas "peligrosamente expuestas, y la mayoría de los clubes viven al borde del desastre financiero". El organismo señala "una peligrosa combinación de creciente deuda y una excesiva dependencia de la financiación de los propietarios, que pone en riesgo a los clubes y a sus aficionados". El éxito económico de la Premier League tampoco ha frenado otro fenómeno: las diferencias financieras entre las distintas categorías y dentro de ellas se han ensanchado de manera considerable. Los números ayudan a entender la dimensión del problema. Diecisiete clubes de la EFL y la National League registrarían pérdidas incluso si sus futbolistas jugaran gratis. El 66% de los equipos no podría sobrevivir más de 90 días sin nueva financiación de sus propietarios y un 29% asegura que ni siquiera alcanzaría los 30 días. Además, el 68% carece de un plan de contingencia para afrontar una posible retirada de su propietario. La IFR considera que "los cimientos de la pirámide están sometidos a una intensa presión y requieren una reforma urgente" y entiende que el informe "debería servir como una llamada de atención" para todo el fútbol inglés. "Diecisiete clubes operan actualmente de tal manera que, si sus jugadores jugaran gratis, sus costes no deportivos les llevarían a la quiebra", declaró David Kogan, presidente de la IFR, a BBC Sport. Su diagnóstico fue todavía más gráfico al hablar de liquidez: "Treinta y dos clubes están funcionando con efectivo suficiente para 30 días. Si el propietario decide no pagar en efectivo a fin de mes, esos clubes quiebran." Kogan añadió: "Ese es un escenario muy, muy arriesgado. Este es el momento de abordar estos problemas antes de que el dinero empiece a escasear." Y resumió la misión que se ha marcado el nuevo organismo: "Podemos arreglar la casa mientras todavía brilla el sol, y ese es esencialmente el papel que vamos a desempeñar en esto." La IFR ha identificado seis áreas de preocupación relacionadas con el riesgo financiero y ha pedido a los clubes que preparen planes de contingencia sólidos ante una posible retirada de la financiación de sus propietarios. El debate llega además en pleno bloqueo entre la Premier League y la EFL, que llevan años negociando sin cerrar un nuevo sistema de financiación para que la máxima categoría comparta más dinero con el resto de divisiones. El regulador posee capacidad para imponer un acuerdo y ya ha dejado clara su posición: "si el fútbol no encuentra una solución, consideraremos los pasos a seguir y no dudaremos en utilizar todos los recursos a nuestro alcance para lograr un cambio duradero". También reclama medidas ante el crecimiento de las pérdidas y exige a los clubes que expliquen cómo incorporan las opiniones de sus aficionados y qué iniciativas están desarrollando para mejorar la diversidad y la gobernanza de sus consejos de administración. Una de las cifras que más llama la atención afecta a la distancia económica entre categorías. El club medio de la Premier League ingresa actualmente más de ocho veces lo que obtiene un equipo medio del Championship. El regulador también pone el foco en los pagos compensatorios que reciben los clubes descendidos desde la Premier. Según el informe, ese modelo "contribuye a incentivar a los clubes del Championship a gastar en exceso, lo que eleva la inflación salarial de los jugadores". A ello se suma un crecimiento de la deuda neta asociada a los traspasos. Los pagos aplazados y la financiación de operaciones crean cada vez más vínculos entre clubes, propietarios y prestamistas, aumentando "el potencial de que el estrés financiero se extienda por todo el deporte". "Nadie en el mundo del fútbol ha creído en los últimos 100 años que este deporte operara en un estado solvente y eficaz", explicó Kogan. "Así no es como ha funcionado nunca el fútbol." El presidente de la IFR considera que el crecimiento de la industria ha multiplicado también los riesgos: "Pero creo que ahora, donde hay mucho más dinero en juego, los extremos se vuelven aún más extremos." Los propios datos sorprendieron al organismo una vez concluido el estudio. "Sabíamos que los problemas existían, pero creo que nadie se dio cuenta de que los datos iban a mostrar lo dramáticos que eran." La Premier League, la EFL, la Federación Inglesa de Fútbol y la Asociación de Aficionados al Fútbol han recibido favorablemente las conclusiones del informe. Otro de los grandes focos está en la financiación de fichajes. Durante los últimos cinco años se ha disparado la práctica de hipotecar las cantidades que un club debe cobrar en el futuro por traspasos para conseguir una inyección inmediata de liquidez. La denominada "financiación de transferencia" se ha convertido en "una fuente de liquidez cada vez más importante". En la temporada 2020-21 ascendía a 55 millones de libras. En la 2024-25 ya alcanzaba los 779 millones, más de 14 veces esa cantidad. En estos momentos se han monetizado aproximadamente 1.200 millones de libras en futuros ingresos por traspasos mediante acuerdos de financiación, casi 22 veces más que en 2020-21. El desequilibrio entre lo que se debe pagar y lo que queda por cobrar también aparece señalado en rojo. En el fútbol inglés, las cantidades pendientes por los fichajes de jugadores son aproximadamente 3,3 veces superiores a los ingresos pendientes por ventas. Durante la temporada 2025-26, los clubes ingleses acumularon cerca de 4.800 millones de libras en cuentas por pagar relacionadas con traspasos y apenas 1.500 millones en cuentas por cobrar. El resultado es una deuda neta por operaciones de mercado de alrededor de 3.300 millones de libras. La situación se vuelve especialmente delicada al bajar desde la Premier. El informe señala un deterioro de las finanzas de los clubes de la EFL y la National League. La mayoría de los equipos del Championship, League One y League Two dispone de efectivo para menos de 30 días. Más del 60% de los clubes de la EFL y la National League tiene pasivos superiores al valor contable de sus activos. El peso de los salarios agrava el cuadro: 20 clubes, principalmente del Championship, League One y National League, dedicaron más del 80% de sus ingresos a pagar las fichas de sus futbolistas. La mayoría de los clubes de League One supera el 40% y existen dos casos que gastan más del 100% de sus ingresos en salarios de jugadores. El crecimiento de los costes laborales se ha extendido por todas las divisiones entre las temporadas 2021-22 y 2025-26. Los salarios aumentaron un 33% en la Premier League, un 32% en el Championship, un 71% en League One y un 63% en League Two. Entre los 18 propietarios de clubes de la EFL encuestados, 17 -el 94%- se declararon partidarios de introducir controles de costes más estrictos. Uno de los inversores consultados lo resumió en el propio informe: "el mayor problema son los salarios de los jugadores". Las pérdidas medias en League One han pasado del 6% de los ingresos en la temporada 1992-93 a casi el 50% en 2024-25. En League Two rondan ya el 40%. La dependencia de los propietarios completa ese escenario. Muchos clubes funcionan con aportaciones periódicas que llegan a lo largo del año justo cuando necesitan liquidez. La mayoría de los equipos de la EFL y la National League tampoco dispone de un plan de contingencia si su propietario deja de financiar las operaciones, una exposición especialmente delicada por el escaso acceso de esos clubes a fuentes alternativas de dinero. "Los clubes de la League One y la League Two recibirán mucha más financiación [a través de un nuevo acuerdo con la Premier League]", afirmó Kogan. "Esos fondos se utilizarán junto con un fondo de desarrollo y un fondo de liquidez, posiblemente para ayudarles a superar las dificultades a las que se enfrentan actualmente". El informe advierte además de que numerosos clubes "no cumplirían actualmente con el requisito de la Ley de Gobernanza del Fútbol de contar con 'recursos financieros adecuados'". Todos tendrán que ajustarse a esa norma antes de mayo de 2030. Kogan considera que los propios dueños ya conocen la magnitud del reto. "Los propietarios son muy conscientes de la necesidad actual de contar con una estructura coherente que permita gestionar los costes", afirmó. El presidente de la IFR aseguró también que el nuevo acuerdo de distribución financiera entre la Premier League y la EFL está cerca de quedar cerrado. La brecha económica tampoco ha dejado de crecer desde el nacimiento de la Premier League. En la temporada 1992-93, un club medio de la máxima categoría ingresaba 10,5 millones de libras, 2,7 veces los 3,9 millones de un club medio del Championship. En 2024-25, el promedio de la Premier había escalado hasta los 341 millones de libras, 8,7 veces los 38,9 millones del segundo escalón. Las diferencias dentro del propio Championship también han aumentado, impulsadas en parte por los pagos compensatorios destinados a los equipos que descienden desde la Premier League. El efecto de esos pagos queda reflejado en la evolución de las cifras. Entre las temporadas 2007-08 y 2025-26, un club del Championship que no acababa de descender de la Premier pasó de recibir 0,9 millones de libras en pagos de solidaridad a percibir 5,3 millones. Para un recién descendido en su primer año, la cantidad creció de 12 millones a 48,7 millones. Esa disparidad alimenta una competición en la que los clubes afrontan realidades financieras muy distintas pese a compartir categoría. La diferencia absoluta de ingresos entre los seis grandes y el resto de la Premier League se ha disparado con el paso de las décadas. En 1992-93, los seis clubes con mayores ingresos ganaban de media 9,4 millones de libras más que el resto. En 2024-25, esa diferencia media había ascendido hasta los 421 millones de libras. Los seis grandes concentran actualmente el 56% de todos los ingresos de la Premier League. El 44% restante queda repartido entre los otros 14 equipos de la competición, otra imagen que completa una radiografía marcada por la concentración de recursos en la cima y la falta de liquidez en buena parte de la pirámide.

articles.title: Paris St-Germain boss Luis Enrique hopes Man City will avoid sanctions
articles.summary: PSG boss Luis Enrique says he was surprised to learn Manchester City had been found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules and  hopes the club avoid sanctions.
articles.body:
Paris St-Germain boss Luis Enrique says he was surprised to learn Manchester City had been found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules and hopes the club can avoid sanctions.

City host European champions PSG in the Champions League on Wednesday (20:00 BST) - their first home match since being found guilty of the majority of 115 charges .

"There is a lot of noise around Manchester City and there is often noise around big clubs," said Enrique when asked about City's guilty verdict at a news conference at Etihad Stadium on Tuesday.

"We just have to wait and see what the final decision will be. I hope everything works out well for Manchester City because I think what they have done on the pitch has been incredible over the last few years and they certainly deserved to win on the pitch all the trophies they have won.

"Now we have to wait to see what the authorities decide or the judge is going to say."

An independent commission found City had broken rules over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018 by creating "sham" contracts with commercial partners to secretly funnel more than £830m into their football operations.

City insist they are innocent and have appealed.

Luis Enrique added: "The first thing that you hear, it is a surprise, but we need to respect the process and wait for the final decision.

"The authorities are responsible for making these decisions. But speaking only about football, they deserved those trophies. I love their football. Beyond that, we have to wait for the decision.

"The trophies you win on the pitch remain on the pitch. They deserved to win that and I hope they can avoid the sanction. But we have to wait."

The star is Luis Enrique - inside the plans to keep PSG at the top

'Criticised for what?' - Maresca defends celebrations

Regulator would quit over Man City interference

Enrique is friends with former City boss Pep Guardiola, who is expected to make his first return to Etihad Stadium on Wednesday since leaving at the end of last season after winning 20 trophies in 10 years.

City were bought for £200m in 2008 by Abu Dhabi United Group, owned by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan - a senior member of the Abu Dhabi ruling family, who is a current vice president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates.

PSG, who have won back-to-back Champions Leagues, are owned by Qatar Sports Investment.

Both City and PSG were fined in 2014 by Uefa for breaching financial rules. PSG insisted at the time they had always operated within the regulations.

Meanwhile, France forward Ousmane Dembele was asked if now was a good time to play City with everything the club is facing off the pitch.

"It is always difficult regardless of it being a good moment or a bad moment," said the PSG attacker.

"They have a high quality team, world-class players and a top coach as well. It doesn't really matter. It's always tough playing Manchester City."

articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Madrid zanjó en la previa del partido ante la Roma los rumores sobre una posible cesión del delantero brasileño, al que considera “muy importante” para el equipo
articles.summary: El entrenador del Madrid zanjó en la previa del partido ante la Roma los rumores sobre una posible cesión del delantero brasileño, al que considera “muy importante” para el equipo
articles.body: José Mourinho despejó cualquier duda sobre el futuro de Endrick en la previa del partido de la Liga de Campeones ante la Roma. Preguntado por TNT acerca de los clubes interesados en el delantero brasileño, el técnico portugués fue tajante y descartó de plano una salida en forma de cesión. “Olvídense, olvídense. Olvídense de los clubes interesados. Es mejor que se sienten a esperar, porque si no se van a cansar”, respondió Mourinho sobre el interés que despierta el futbolista. El entrenador dejó claro el concepto que tiene de él: “Es un jugador que adoro. Es un jugador que creo que tiene un potencial increíble y es muy importante para nosotros”. Mourinho también se refirió a la situación que ha vivido Endrick desde el inicio de la temporada, marcada por una lesión. “Después de la pretemporada, tuvo una lesión que lo apartó más de un mes, cuatro o cinco semanas, que lo apartó del inicio de la temporada. Yo mismo ya he hablado con él, porque después de recuperarse todavía no se había dado la ocasión”, explicó. El portugués puso como ejemplo el reciente encuentro ante el Villarreal para ilustrar la falta de minutos del brasileño. “Este partido, para nuestra suerte, fue su mala suerte, porque cuando hacemos el gol, él iba a entrar. Él y Bernardo iban a entrar prácticamente en el momento en que hacemos el gol. Y después, ganando y con diez, es normal que un entrenador cambie de idea y tenga otras opciones”, detalló, en alusión a la expulsión de Vinicius que condicionó sus planes. Mourinho cerró su intervención con una declaración de intenciones sobre la continuidad del delantero. “Quien esté interesado en él va a tener que pelear mucho conmigo, porque creo que no necesita salir cedido y que va a tener el mayor de los éxitos aquí”, sentenció.

articles.summary: Atletico Madrid's captain Koke faces a heartbreaking loss with the death of his mother just before the Champions League match against Manchester United. Both clubs pay tribute.
articles.body: Atletico Madrid captain Koke has suffered a devastating family loss just hours before his side faces Manchester United in the Champions League, with the Spanish club confirming that his mother, Ana Merodio Borja, died in Madrid on Tuesday. The news has cast a shadow over the fixture at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano, with both clubs paying tribute to the midfielder’s family and arrangements made for a minute’s silence before kick-off.Atletico confirm Koke’s mother has diedAtletico Madrid announced the death of Ana Merodio Borja, mother of first-team captain Koke and under-19 assistant coach Borja Resurrección, without disclosing a cause of death. The news means Koke will miss Tuesday evening’s Champions League fixture against Manchester United, as the club and its supporters come together to support the family.In a statement, Atletico confirmed that UEFA had authorised tributes at both the senior team’s match and the UEFA Youth League fixture involving the clubs’ youth sides. The club’s under-19 team observed a minute’s silence earlier on Tuesday, with players wearing black armbands alongside their opponents.Atletico also confirmed that the flag outside the Metropolitano was flying at half-mast as a mark of respect for Koke’s mother.“Tonight, before the start of our Champions League match against Manchester United, a minute's silence will be observed in memory of Ana Merodio Borja, mother of our captain, Koke, who passed away this morning in Madrid,” the club said.“Our club requested permission from UEFA to observe a minute's silence both during the first team match and the UEFA Youth League game, as well as for the players to wear black armbands.”The statement continued: “Atlético de Madrid would like to express our deepest condolences to all his family and friends, and especially to Koke, captain of the first team, and Borja Resurrección, assistant coach of the Juvenil A team. Rest in peace.”Manchester United offer condolences ahead of kick-offManchester United also issued a statement expressing their sympathy for Koke and his family, while asking supporters travelling to Madrid to join both teams in observing the minute’s silence before the Champions League match.“Manchester United is saddened by the passing of Ana Merodio Borja, beloved mother of Atletico de Madrid captain Koke and U19s assistant coach Borja Resurrección,” the club said.“We offer our condolences to the family at this difficult time and invite supporters to join the two teams in a minute’s silence ahead of kick-off tonight.”The tribute comes as United prepare for a challenging away fixture against Atletico, with both teams looking to improve their positions in the Champions League standings. articles.title: Man City charges: Ahead of PSG, Dias defends celebrations at Liverpool
articles.summary: Captain Ruben Dias says the Manchester City players trust the club and celebrations after win at Anfield were justified.
articles.body:
Manchester City captain Ruben Dias said on Tuesday that “people don’t love us winning and we love to win”, as he robustly defended his football club’s raucous celebrations after beating Liverpool, despite being found guilty of a catalogue of Premier League financial rules breaches.

City were jeered throughout by Liverpool fans during a 3-0 win at Anfield last weekend that left them top of the Premier League table, three points clear of reigning champions Arsenal, with six wins from six matches.

It was City’s first game since being found guilty of more than 100 charges relating to breaches of the English top flight’s financial fair-play rules.

City have appealed the verdict, with every match featuring the team now played under a huge cloud of uncertainty.

Manager Enzo Maresca’s men will be back in European action on Wednesday when they play at home against holders Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) in the Champions League.

Both clubs are bankrolled by wealthy owners from the Gulf, with City backed by the ruling family of Abu Dhabi while PSG are financed by the Qatari state.

“I really feel like I speak for the whole group; we trust the club,” insisted Dias, despite City being found guilty of 34 charges of failing to cooperate with the league’s investigation.

The Portugal defender added: “If there’s more or less noise or whatever the reason the noise is, at the end of the day it’s all the same, same as before, because people don’t love us winning and we love to win.”

City faced criticism for the exuberant way they celebrated victory over 10-man Liverpool.

But an unapologetic Maresca said, “Criticised for what? We won 3-0 at Anfield. What do you want us to do? Even if it was 1-0, it would be exactly the same.

“We work every day to win games. It’s the only thing that we can think about and be focused [on].”

Dias backed Maresca by saying, “To win at Anfield in whatever circumstance, whether it’s earlier in the season or later in the season, we will enjoy it just as much.

“We will celebrate however it feels in the moment, and it will obviously be a show of how much it means to us.”

Maresca added that the fallout from the guilty verdicts was more difficult for City supporters to deal with than for his squad.

“Probably it has been more tough for our fans than for the players or for me,” he said.

“It is more complicated because if I was an Arsenal fan or United fan and you are a City fan, I can say ‘My friend, you are a cheat’ or these kinds of things. So probably, it has been more tough for them.”

PSG are bidding for a third straight Champions League title, having come from two goals down to beat City 4-2 in stunning fashion during the 2024-25 edition.

“The message for tomorrow night is quite easy, in terms of winning the perfect game because they [PSG] are the best team in Europe in this moment,” said Maresca.

“They won the last two Champions Leagues, so that shows how good they are. So we need the perfect game, but at the same time doing our best, I think we can beat them and be happy at the end.”

Former City manager Pep Guardiola is due to attend Wednesday’s game in what will be his first visit to the Etihad since standing down at the end of last season, with the Spaniard having already publicly backed his old club during the current crisis.

“I spoke with Pep after the [Manchester] United game,” said Maresca.

“In case he’s coming, it’s a nice feeling – especially for him, because this has been his house for 10 years with what he has done here. It’s exciting for everyone.”

articles.title: EA Sports' College Football Devs Reportedly Fear the Franchise Could Disappear by 2030
articles.summary: Developers working on EA Sports' College Football franchise reportedly fear that the series may not live to see the end of the decade.
articles.body:
Developers working on EA Sports' College Football franchise reportedly fear that the series may not live to see the end of the decade.

The report comes from Insider Gaming's Mike Straw , who spoke to senior-level sources working on or around the football series. He noted that, although the series is performing well, sales have gradually declined entry to entry since its highly-anticipated debut in 2024. While this isn't inherently a bad thing (or unexpected, given the extreme hype around the 2024 title), costs associated with the game have been rising.

Per the report, in 2024, EA paid each player featured in the game $600, amounting to roughly $7 million total. Those costs have tripled, with NIL (name, image, likeness) rights for college athletes now costing $1,500 per player. As a result, EA spent roughly $20 million on its players with its latest game. EA also pays boatloads of cash to license bowl games, universities, and more, meaning tens of millions of dollars goes into just having the right to use certain elements in the game as opposed to raw development costs.

EA Sports College Football 27 - Dynasty Screenshots and GIFs

This has led to EA trying to monetize key areas of the game, including College Football's single-player modes. This led to extreme backlash earlier this summer due to the fact players felt they were being pushed to pay to efficently play single-player content. EA eventually bent the knee and reversed course , but noted that it would retool these options and bring them back in future entries.

One source told Insider Gaming that microtransactions were planned to return in future College Football single-player titles, and feared that it would anger players, pushing them away from a game that is trying to grow. While there are College Football games planned for the next few years, sources reportedly fear that the franchise may be on its way out.

"We’re not FC. We’re not Madden. We don’t make the money they do, and everyone knows it," a source told Insider Gaming. "But it’s at the point where if we don’t find a way to keep players around and, in turn, make more, we won’t have anything. Forget in 10 years, I’m scared about if we have a game by the end of the decade. Games aren’t getting cheaper to make, and there’s the real concern with all of us that EA’s going to streamline and just have a few key franchises and dump everything else."

Insider Gaming noted that not all of its sources shared these fears and some believed there is a strong future with the franchise. EA Sports' College Football brand is a spiritual successor to EA Sports' highly popular NCAA football series that thrived in the 2000s and early 2010s before legal issues surrounding NIL rights effectively killed it. There was a 14-year gap between NCAA's final game and the debut of the new College Football series, which led to an extreme level of enthusiasm from fans.

It led to College Football 25 raking in big bucks and becoming the second best selling game of 2024 in the United States, though it hasn't sustained that momentum year-to-year. College Football 26 was the seventh best selling game in the United States in 2025, with College Football 27 currently placed in 10th this year. Of course, College Football also doesn't have as much global appeal as something like EA's FC series, which means its sales are primarily made up in the US.

articles.body: Como no podía ser de otra manera, el inicio del partido entre el Atlético y el Manchester United estuvo presidido por un minuto para honrar la memoria de Ana Merodio Borja, la madre de Koke y Borja Resurrección. Un emotivo silencio, al que se unieron también los más de 3.000 aficionados ingleses, que encogió los corazones... y que tuvo prolongación nada más sonar el pitido del árbitro. Así, tras echar a rodar el balón, y con la emoción aún a flor de piel, el Atlético se lanzaría a rendirle un homenaje a la familia del capitán y del segundo entrenador del Juvenil A, precisando sólo 53 segundos. Fue lo que tardaría Barrios en enviar a la red una gran asistencia de Baena. Brazos al cielo desde donde también lo ve todo la madre del 8 y seis dedos en alusión a Koke, convirtiendo la celebración en otro momento más sobrecogedor aún. Eso sí, tras recibir los abrazos de sus compañeros en el córner más alejado del banquillo, a Barrios no le daría tiempo a acudir a la banda, donde le esperaban con una camiseta de la máxima leyenda rojiblanca. Daba igual, el mensaje de apoyo ya estaba dado. El técnico del Atlético no puedo evitar las lágrimas en un momento de mucha emoción también para él. Koke es el futbolista que más partidos ha jugado con Simeone como entrenador rojiblanco y su relación y unión con el capitán es más que evidente.

articles.title: Georgia Tech's Kyle Efford Retires Due to Injuries, All-ACC LB Says He Gave 'Everything I Had in Me'
articles.summary: Georgia Tech two-time All-ACC linebacker Kyle Efford is medically retiring from football, he announced Tuesday.
articles.body:
Georgia Tech two-time All-ACC linebacker Kyle Efford is medically retiring from football, he announced Tuesday.

"Over the past few years, my body has taken more damage than I can continue to ignore... and while my heart and my mind still have so much more to give, I reached a point where I have to start thinking about the life ahead of me," Efford told reporters (h/t Fletcher Page of the Atlanta Journal-Constitution ).

Efford continued, "This isn't how I imagined my football career coming to an end, but I'm at peace because I can say with full confidence that I gave this game everything that I had in me."

Efford, who was in his fifth season with Georgia Tech, missed games earlier this fall. He returned last Saturday to record a tackle for loss in a 28-25 win over Duke.

He will retire as a two-year team captain who recorded 250 career tackles over parts of six seasons with the Yellow Jackets.

Efford added 6.5 sacks, three passes defensed, a forced fumble and an interception across 43 games. The fifth-year senior will remain with Georgia Tech this season as a captain and player-coach, according to the team .

"We'll miss having No. 44 in the middle of our defense, but know that he'll continue to make an impact on this team with his leadership and presence," Yellow Jackets coach Brent Key said in a statement.

Efford previously missed time and played through a shoulder injury in 2024 before undergoing surgery the following offseason.

He missed time again this season after injuring his shoulder during Georgia Tech's Week 2 overtime win against Tennessee.

Efford led the Yellow Jackets in tackles in each of the last three seasons, becoming the program's first player in 24 years to accomplish the feat.

He racked up 81 tackles during his freshman 2023 season to become the first freshman in 23 years to lead the Yellow Jackets in tackles.

He added 64 tackles despite injury limitations in 2024, then paced his team once more with 77 tackles in 2025.

Efford recorded 27 tackles, including two for loss, to go along with a sack this season despite being limited to 169 defensive snaps over three games. He capped off his career with six tackles in last weekend's win over Duke.

Georgia Tech's season will continue Saturday with a road game against Virginia Tech.

articles.title: Kolkata to bring El Clasico to India with blockbuster Barcelona vs Real Madrid Legends clash on Nov 25: Luis Figo, Puyol among expected names
articles.summary: Kolkata will host a thrilling El Clasico exhibition match featuring Barcelona and Real Madrid legends on November 25, with expected appearances from Luis Figo and Carles Puyol. Fans can relive the historic rivalry of these two Spanish football giants in an exciting event at the Salt Lake Stadium.
articles.body: Kolkata is preparing for another taste of El Clasico, with Barcelona and Real Madrid legends set to bring their famous rivalry to India on November 25. The exhibition will give fans another chance to see former stars of the Spanish giants together on Indian soil, following Real Madrid Legends’ victory in Mumbai last year. With Luis Figo, Carles Puyol and Iker Casillas among the names reportedly expected, the contest could be a significant occasion for a city with a long relationship with world football.Kolkata to host Barcelona vs Real Madrid LegendsWest Bengal sports minister Indranil Khan announced on Tuesday that Barcelona Legends and Real Madrid Legends will meet at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan, popularly known as the Salt Lake Stadium, on November 25.The official squads have not yet been confirmed, although Portuguese great Figo, who represented both Spanish rivals during his playing career, and former Barcelona captain Puyol are among the prominent names expected to feature, alongside Spain’s World Cup-winning goalkeeper Casillas.This will be the second time the two clubs’ legends have faced each other in India, following their meeting at Mumbai’s DY Patil Stadium last year. Real Madrid Legends won that contest 2-0, with former striker Fernando Morientes and David Barral scoring the goals.The two sides also met in Miami earlier in 2026, playing out a 1-1 draw in which Martin Montoya scored for Barcelona and Álvaro Negredo found the net for Real Madrid. Their Kolkata encounter will now bring the exhibition rivalry to another Indian city, with the final line-ups still to be confirmed.For supporters, the appeal lies in seeing familiar names from two of football’s most celebrated clubs share the same pitch again. Figo’s unusual connection to both sides adds another layer of interest, while the prospect of Puyol and Casillas appearing gives fans further reason to watch for the official team announcements.Barcelona return to Kolkata after eight yearsBarcelona’s visit will mark their first appearance in Kolkata since September 2018, when they faced Indian football giants Mohun Bagan at the same stadium. The Catalans won that match 6-0, with Javier Saviola, Roger Garcia, Pedro Landi, Jari Litmanen and Jofre Mateu among the scorers.Kolkata has hosted some of football’s biggest names over several decades, earning a reputation as one of India’s most devoted footballing cities. One of its most memorable occasions came in 1977, when Brazilian legend Pelé led New York Cosmos against Mohun Bagan at Eden Gardens, while German giants Bayern Munich visited the city in 2008 to play the Kolkata club in a friendly.The city also hosted Lionel Messi’s only appearance on Indian soil in 2011, when Argentina faced Venezuela at the Salt Lake Stadium. More recently, the venue staged high-profile international friendlies in early October 2026, as India faced five-time world champions Brazil and two-time World Cup winners Uruguay.The November exhibition will add another prominent fixture to that history, bringing together two clubs whose rivalry has captivated football supporters across generations. El 10 del Barça se inventó un regate que dio lugar al 1-3 de Gordon ante el Galatasaray con el que sacó de ritmo a Elmali, su marcador, tan fuera del espacio y del tiempo con el truco del español que le acabó sirviendo de asistente involuntario, como en los espectáculos de magia. Lamine encaró el área por la derecha, se fue a línea de fondo y desde allí amagó con soltar una rabona que acabó abortando para dejar en el sitio a Elmali. Con el rival tieso, su siguiente paso no fue bueno y fue el turco el que, en un mal toque, le dejó el balón muerto para asistir desde la cal a Gordon, que le pegó al palo corto. No era la primera asistencia de Lamine en Estambul. El 1-2 también nació en sus botas, en un centro tocadito y maravilloso que Fermín cabeceó a la red. Y pudieron ser más, porque en otro toque de genio dejó solito a Gordon, que falló a puerta vacía. Elmali ya tenía malos recuerdos de Lamine Yamal, que le hizo la vida imposible en aquel 0-6 que le endosó España a Turquía en Konya hace poco más de un año.

articles.title: El Villarreal se quedó con nueve jugadores por la nueva norma contra las pérdidas de tiempo
articles.standfirst: El árbitro dejó a Freeman y Oluwaseyi casi dos minutos en la banda al considerar que Gerard y Mikautadze habían tardado más de diez segundos en abandonar el terreno de juego
articles.summary: El árbitro dejó a Freeman y Oluwaseyi un minuto en la banda al considerar que Gerard y Mikautadze habían tardado más de diez segundos en abandonar el terreno de juego
articles.body: Una de las imágenes más llamativas del encuentro de Liga de Campeones entre el Villarreal y el Nápoles llegó en el minuto 63, cuando el conjunto castellonense se quedó de forma momentánea con solo nueve futbolistas sobre el terreno de juego por la aplicación de una de las nuevas normas arbitrales impulsadas por la International Football Association Board (IFAB). La decisión fue adoptada por el árbitro alemán Daniel Siebert durante una doble sustitución ordenada por el técnico amarillo, Iñigo Pérez. Gerard Moreno y Mikautadze abandonaban el campo para dejar su sitio a Freeman y Oluwaseyi, pero los dos relevos tuvieron que permanecer en la banda sin autorización para entrar mientras el juego continuaba. La escena provocó una sonora bronca en La Cerámica. El público mostró su incomprensión, mientras el banquillo del Villarreal y los responsables del club reclamaban explicaciones al colegiado y, sobre todo, al cuarto árbitro. Durante casi dos minutos el equipo castellonense tuvo que competir con dos futbolistas menos hasta que el juego se detuvo, después de que se hubiera cumplido un minuto a tiempo corrido. La actuación arbitral se ajustó, sin embargo, al nuevo protocolo de sustituciones con límite de tiempo introducido por la IFAB dentro de la Regla 3 de las Reglas de Juego. La medida pretende combatir las pérdidas deliberadas de tiempo y evitar que los cambios se utilicen para enfriar el ritmo de los partidos. La normativa establece que, una vez mostrado el panel de sustitución, el jugador que abandona el terreno de juego dispone de un máximo de diez segundos para salir por el punto más cercano de la línea de banda o de fondo. En caso de sustituciones múltiples, todos los futbolistas reemplazados deben haber abandonado el campo dentro de ese mismo plazo contado desde la señalización del último cambio.

articles.title: Mastantuono, operado de una mano
articles.standfirst: El argentino se dañó en el encuentro ante el Genoa
articles.summary: El argentino se dañó en el encuentro ante el Genoa
articles.body: Franco Mastantuono ha sido operado para "reducir y reparar una fractura del cuarto metacarpiano de la mano izquierda", según informa el parte médico de la Fiorentina. El jugador argentino, propiedad del Real Madrid y cedido en el conjunto italiano, se hizo daño en la mano en el partido ante el Genoa y ha requerido de una intervención quirúrgica para reparar su lesión. Pese a lo aparatoso del comunicado médico, la Fiorentina asegura que estará disponible para el próximo encuentro del conjunto viola, el domingo ante el Como (15.00 horas) La ACF Fiorentina anuncia que esta tarde el jugador Franco Mastantuono fue intervenido quirúrgicamente de forma ambulatoria para reducir y reparar una fractura del cuarto metacarpiano de la mano izquierda, sufrida tras un traumatismo contundente durante el partido de liga entre el Genoa y la Fiorentina. El jugador retomará su actividad habitual con el equipo mañana y estará disponible para el próximo partido de liga.
