articles.title: Richarlison: Goal crisis & drop zone - so why is Spurs' £60m man stuck in U21s?
articles.summary: After being left out of Tottenham's Premier League squad last month, Richarlison has been left to feature for the under-21s side
articles.body:
Less than four years after representing Brazil at the 2022 World Cup, Richarlison's downward spiral at Tottenham was laid bare as he scored in front of a couple of hundred supporters for the under-21s against Cheltenham Town in the EFL Trophy.

The Brazilian, who cost Spurs £60m from Everton and was rubbing shoulders with Neymar Jr and Vinicius Jr on international duty not so long ago, looked almost embarrassed to celebrate his thumping half-volley against the League Two outfit.

He also notched a penalty in a shootout that Spurs' reserves lost 7-6 after a 2-2 draw.

Richarlison, 29, was making only his second appearance of the season, and his first since the end of August against Brentford, having been left out of Tottenham's Premier League squad.

Manager Roberto de Zerbi insisted the decision to omit him from the club's 25-man squad in September was not his, following the forward's failed move back to Merseyside at the end of the transfer window.

With just three goals, Spurs are the top-flight's lowest scorers this season and second bottom in the table. So the decision to leave last season's 12-goal leading scorer out of their league plans looks increasingly difficult to justify.

EFL Trophy offers rare chance of minutes

For a couple of hours on transfer deadline day, it seemed only a matter of time before Richarlison left Tottenham.

He was closing in on an idyllic return to Everton, more than four years after swapping Merseyside for North London.

But after expressing his desire to depart, a proposed move to the Hill Dickinson Stadium fell through, leaving both the player and club with few alternatives at such a late stage of the summer transfer window.

"He decided everything alone," De Zerbi said in September. "He spoke with me at the beginning of the pre-season and told me his idea and desire was to leave.

"At the end we go to bring another striker [in] and, like I said at the beginning of the pre-season, I want to keep the players, just the players that want to stay and be proud and with the right passion to stay here.

"Then for everything and other problems, it is not my business and not my job. It is the responsibility of the club.

"I can't say nothing because I didn't decide anything. The message of Richarlison from the beginning of the season has been very clear. I accepted that and for me [there is] nothing [to say]."

Later that month, a proposed move to Brazilian side Vasco da Gama also fell through after Richarlison failed to agree personal terms.

He was also ruled out of Spurs' Carabao Cup tie against Liverpool last month, with only players registered in their club's respective league squad eligible to feature in the competition.

The ex-Watford forward may now have to get used to the surroundings of English football's lower leagues, with the EFL Trophy's group stage offering him a rare opportunity to gain competitive minutes before January.

Solanke struggles highlight attacking concern

Just six games into the new Premier League season, Tottenham may already be regretting their decision not to register Richarlison.

Since arriving from Everton, he has scored 27 top-flight goals in 103 appearances.

He was also Tottenham's leading scorer in the competition last season, netting 11 times in 32 appearances as they narrowly avoided relegation to the Championship.

Dominic Solanke's late equaliser against Manchester United on Saturday was the first Premier League goal from a Tottenham forward since Richarlison netted against Chelsea back in May.

Former England striker Alan Shearer questioned Solanke's quality on Match of the Day, describing him as "nowhere near good enough" - the 29-year-old has scored just 13 league goals since joining two years ago from Bournemouth in a £55m deal.

De Zerbi, though, was pleased with Solanke's performance and contribution after his first goal of the season rescued a point at Old Trafford despite Spurs being reduced to 10 men.

But despite the Italian's positive view and faith in his frontman, Tottenham's problems in the final third are difficult to ignore, having spent £300m on new recruits over the summer.

When they failed to score in their first four Premier League games this term, supporters inside the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium were holding banners begging the 2025 Europa League winners to find the net.

Richarlison might not provide the answer to all of his side's problems, but his inclusion in the Premier League squad would surely have been more beneficial than allowing him to trudge around the pitches of England's lower-tier clubs and show his finishing prowess in front of sparse crowds.

articles.title: Arteta le gana la partida a Davide Ancelotti en siete minutos
articles.standfirst: El conjunto 'gunner' supera al Lille con tres tantos seguidos en un encuentro que dominó de principio a fin
articles.summary: El conjunto 'gunner' supera al Lille con tres tantos seguidos en un encuentro que dominó de principio a fin
articles.body: El Arsenal volvía al Emirates Stadium para vivir su estreno en casa en la presente temporada de la Champions League. Arteta apostó de inicio por Mikel Merino y su pegada. Un encuentro correoso que tuvo que esperar al 64' para ver el primer tanto de Timber y justo después el gol de Eze apenas tres minutos después. Una locura de segunda mitad en la que también apareció Saka para poner el tercero y definitivo del partido. Un Arsenal que comenzó dominando el esférico con posesiones largas y un Lille que no apretaba demasiado arriba. Lo intentaba el conjunto gunner con las internadas de Madueke y Eze por las bandas, pero sin mucho éxito en el tramo inicial de encuentro. El guion de los franceses pasaba por encerrarse atrás y salir con todo a la contra. El muro del Lille era digno del más puro catennacio italiano. Todos bien replegados y que no entrara nadie. Gyokeres no olía el esférico y lo notaba el conjunto gunner que no encontraba a su referencia arriba. La primera llegada de peligro para el Arsenal llegó en las botas de Bruno Guimarães y su disparo con la zurda que se fue algo desviado de la portería de Ozer. El primer susto del Lille llegó con el gol anulado a Ueda. Estaba algo adelantado en la posición en la que le llegó el balón y el tanto no subió al marcador. Lo probó Merino con un par de disparos, pero el internacional no encontraba portería como sí lo hace con la selección española. Un Arsenal que llegó al descanso sin poder marcar ningún tanto con la gran actividad de la zaga francesa. Comenzó el Arsenal la segunda mitad con la intención de apretar desde el primer momento. Muchas llegadas que se convertían en córners y jugadas de peligro. La cuestión es que el muro del conjunto francés ya comenzaba a ser demasiado para los pupilos de Arteta que se frustraban con el paso de los minutos. El conjunto de Londres proponía muy poco ante la solidez del Lille... hasta que Timber perforara la portería de Ozer con una 'picadita' de muchos quilates y Eze anotara un zurdazo gracias a la asistencia del recién ingresado al campo Saka. Protagonista también de meter el tercer y definitivo tanto del Arsenal en una ráfaga ofensiva total. Lo que comenzó a ser muro pasó a ser un agujero en el que el conjunto gunner aprovechó por muchos huecos con las sustituciones de Arteta. Una recta final en la que el Arsenal trató de adormecer el encuentro con muchos pases y la dirección de Odegaard en el centro del campo. Un Lille que se marcharía del Emirates con un juego muy discreto y sin apenas ocasiones.

articles.title: Hay que decirlo claro: la estrella de este Atlético es Pablo Barrios
articles.standfirst: La contra crónica del Atlético-Manchester United.
articles.summary: La contra crónica del Atlético-Manchester United.
articles.body: Es el mejor. Y cada vez hay menos debate dentro y fuera del Atlético. Hablamos de un Pablo Barrios que, cuando la salud le respeta, es el jugador más diferencial de la plantilla. El que otorga esa salto de calidad necesario a un grupo que tiene muchos jugadores de primer nivel, pero ninguno como el 8. Quizá Julián, cuando recupere su mejor versión, pueda mirarle cara a cara. Pero sin Griezmann... nadie más. De ahí que Simeone le cuide como le cuida. Le volvió a sacar del campo a la hora tras preguntarle si le cambiaba. Bruno Fernandes es uno de los mejores jugadores de Europa de la úlrima década. Tanto con el Manchester United, donde es una leyenda y el capitán, como con Portugal, donde ha sido siempre intocable. Por eso llama la atención verle desesperado en muchas acciones de un equipo que está muy lejos de la gloria del pasado. Por mucho dinero que gasten han perdido grandeza y parece que costará recuperarla. Eso sí, dejó un detallazo en la segunda parte con un balón al larguero. Primer partido en el Metropolitano desde el derbi. Primer partido para evaluar los decibelios de la afición contra Julián. Si ante el Madrid fue una pitada histórica, frente al Manchester United se rebajó de manera considerable. El paso del tiempo está enfriando la inquina de la grada con el argentino, que incluso fue aplaudido en alguna acción realizada durante el partido. Eso sí, cuando fue reemplazado en el minuto 72 se volvió a llevar otra bronca. Que el Cuti Romero es un líder se sabía desde antes de llegar al Atlético. su trayectoria a nivel de clubes y con Argentina así lo definían. Pero es que el central lo es en todo. Hasta en detalles como el acontecido en el minuto 30. Una jugada de ataque rojiblanco que acabó con el defensa en el suelo reclamando penalti. Volvió a defender, pero fue al colegiado a reclamarle la pena máxima. Ser un líder también es saber presionar a los árbitros. Apenas 12 minutos después de arrancar el partido se produjo una de esas jugadas que valen una entrada. Un recorte, caño incluido, de Mbeumo que dejó sentado a Cuti Romero. No es fácil marcharse así de uno de los mejores centrales del mundo, no es sencillo dejarle clavado de esta manera. Ojo a este camerunés que es de esos futbolistas que merece la pena seguir. Ni un minuto tardó Barrios, que marcó el 1-0, en homenajear a Koke. Un minuto, precisamente, de silencio más que emotivo por el fallecimiento de la madre del capitán. Una leyenda que hoy ha vivido uno de los días más difíciles de su vida. Una leyenda que ha visto como todo el estadio respetaba el homenaje y después coreaba su nombre. DEP doña Ana Merodio.

articles.title: Tresoldi estelariza una auténtica noche de Brujas en Milán
articles.standfirst: El italo-alemán firma un soberbio 'hat-trick' en el Giuseppe Meazza
articles.summary: El italo-alemán firma un soberbio 'hat-trick' en el Giuseppe Meazza
articles.body: Dos partidos, dos derrotas. El Inter sucumbió en Milán ante un brillante Brujas en una velada que fue tan oda al fútbol ofensivo como insulto a la memoria de las grandes defensas del 'Calcio'. Ambos equipos acumularon más de 45 disparos y Sommer se hizo grande en la que, hasta este verano, era su casa. Un 'hat-trick' de Nicolò Tresoldi, nacido en Cerdeña, sepultó a un vigente campeón de Italia que entra en barrena en Europa. Obligado a ganar en casa tras su derrota en el Bernabéu, el Inter de Chivu salió al ataque en el Giuseppe Meazza contra un Brujas que no se arrugó. Si bien la primera fue para Marcus Thuram, los belgas fueron creciendo con el paso de los minutos y Forbs le 'sacó' un penalti a un Calhanoglu que llegó tarde tras una brutal carrera desde campo propio. Tresoldi, que sigue dudando entre jugar con Alemania o Italia, transformó la pena máxima por toda la escuadra. Empezaron a llegar las dudas en Milán y Chivu, consternado en el banquillo, se enfadaba por los problemas defensivos evidentes que muestra su equipo. Pero los 'nerazzurri' tiraron de carácter para meterse de nuevo en el duelo. Lautaro ejerció de capitán y, tras ver cómo le anulaban el empate por fuera de juego, hizo el 1-1 antes del descanso con una gran maniobra para quedarse solo ante Sommer. No falló. Sin embargo, las limitaciones de este Inter en ambas áreas son muy grandes... y en Champions, pasan factura. Ni la nariz fracturada de Mechele o la lesión de Spileers 'ayudaron' a los italianos. Lautaro perdonó lo imperdonable y Tresoldi, en la que quizás sea su casa en el futuro, se puso las botas. El italo-germano destrozó a un Inter que se deshacía en defensa con el paso de los minutos. Primero, aprovechó un error clamoroso de Josep Martínez (otro) saliendo del área; después, firmó el 'hat-trick' empujando a gol un rechace para firmar su noveno tanto del curso. Un sardo que juega con Alemania Sub21 desataba una auténtica noche de Brujas en Milán. Sacó carácter Lautaro para hacer el 2-3 a poco más de 10 minutos del final, y tuvo el Inter el empate... pero Vermant finiquitó al contragolpe ante un equipo completamente roto. El tanto de Bonny, el 3-4 final, anotado ya en el descuento, fue una mera anécdota. El Giuseppe Meazza, ocho meses después de ver la eliminación de su equipo en Europa ante el Bodo/Glimt, vuelve a vivir una dramática noche europea.

articles.title: Gruda regatea el primer 0-0 de la Champions y sirve la primera victoria para Demichelis
articles.standfirst: El talentoso mediapunta alemán le dio la victoria al Leipzig contra el PSV (1-0) en la segunda parte
articles.summary: El talentoso mediapunta alemán le dio la victoria al Leipzig contra el PSV (1-0) en la segunda parte
articles.body: Antes o después, acabará llegando... pero no será esta vez. Y es que, cuando el primer 0-0 de esta edición de la Champions comenzaba a 'asomar la patita', el talentoso Brajan Gruda sacó su zurda a pasear para darle la victoria al Leipzig contra el PSV (1-0). Demichelis introdujo tres novedades respecto al once que se estrenó cayendo goleado ante el Como: Banzuzi acompañó a El Aynaoui en el doble pivote; Gruda arrancó en derecha; y Romulo le quitó el punto a Guiu arriba. También realizó ajustes un Peter Bosz que incrustó a Mauro Júnior en la medular y ubicó a Mijnans como falso '9'. Yarek, un día más, arrancó desde el banquillo. Arrancó el encuentro con trabajo para Kovar y Vandervoordt en ambas porterías. El meta del PSV tiró de reflejos para sacar una mano a volea de Nkunku desde el interior del área, mientras que el meta belga tuvo que estirarse para repeler un remate cruzado a cargo de Mijnans poco después. El choque pudo empezar a romperse nada más superar el primer cuarto de hora cuando, en su intento por cerrar un centro buscando a Ruben van Bommel en el segundo palo, tocó el balón con la mano. Asumió la responsabilidad un veterano de guerra como Perisic. Pero, a pesar de vencerse para un lado, Vandevoordt 'estiró la pata' para desviar el lanzamiento del croata. El centro del campo se limitó a ser una zona de paso. Nada fuera de lo normal teniendo en cuenta la propuesta que suele caracterizar a ambos conjuntos. A los puntos, sin embargo, el Leipzig hizo más méritos para haber podido inclinar el marcador al descanso. Sobre todo, desde el desequilibrio de Gruda y Nusa por fuera. Kovar, de nuevo, se apuntó la primera intervención del segundo tiempo a 'zurdazo' de Nusa directo a su entrepierna. Ruben van Bommel, apretando el acelerador a fondo, respondió desbordando por izquierda y cediendo un balón atrás para la llegada de un Mijnans que abrió demasiado el pie. Acto seguido, Kostic conectó un remate seco que Vandervoordt se quitó de encima y, de vuelta, Kovar sacó a córner otro intento de Baku tras un 'taconazo' exquisito de Gruda. El ida y vuelta era constante. En esta ocasión, fue Dest quien apareció por sorpresa desde el lateral derecho para probar suerte y, de nuevo, apareció Kovar para realizar una doble intervención de tremendo mérito. No había manera de superar a Vandervoordt y Kovar. Pero, a un cuarto de hora para el pitido final, a Gruda le cayó un balón en la corona del área y, con ayuda del desvío de un defensor, puso el 1-0 en el marcador. Yarek, que entró desde el banquillo, mandó un 'cabezazo' a la madera y, poco después, se le anuló un gol a Obispo por fuera de juego. Sufrió el Leipzig a la hora de defender el aluvión de centros laterales que comenzó a lanzar el PSV. Lukeba, incluso, se libró de cometer un penalti por mano porque el balón venía de un rebote. Acabó embotellado en su propio área. Pero, finalmente, los de Demichalis lograron llevarse sus tres primeros puntos.

articles.title: El Villarreal supera el mal de la Champions con una victoria a lo grande ante el Nápoles
articles.standfirst: Mikautadze, Mouriño y Oluwaseyi remontan el tanto inicial de Rrahmani y suman la primera victoria en los últimos diez partidos de la máxima competición
articles.summary: Mikautadze, Mouriño y Oluwaseyi remontan el tanto inicial de Rrahmani y suman la primera victoria en los últimos diez partidos de la máxima competición
articles.body: El Villarreal se superó a sí mismo y a su mal de altura en la Champions gracias a una victoria de autoridad con remontada ante un Nápoles que se adelantó en el marcador, pero que metió al submarino en el partido con un error impropio de la competición. El equipo de Iñigo Pérez aprovechó el regalo de la primera parte para lograr una remontada exprés y, después, supo competir para no dejar escapar la renta y sentenciar el partido al final. Le costó al Villarreal activarse al modo Champions, la competición que te mide a rivales que hacen brotar una ocasión de gol de un erial. Fue en ese tramo de partido en el que aún no se han sentado todos los espectadores en sus butacas cuando el Nápoles intimidó más por apariencia que por fuego real. Y no fue la prevista lucha por las bandas, ni la batalla táctica en el centro del campo la que inclinó el partido. Una jugada de pizarra de Allegri, un córner con dos toques en corto, sorprendió a la defensa del Villarreal. Gilmour centró al área y Rrahmani marcó tras un primer paradón entre Luiz Júnior y el larguero. El submarino respondió con buenas ocasiones, especialmente con un disparo de Mikautadze que desvió Badiashile a córner haciéndole un favor a su portero. Luego lo intentaron Carlos Romero, Gueye, Gerard y Renato Veiga. Todos finalizaban las jugadas con disparos con buena dirección, pero no entre los palos. El Nápoles se recompuso con la omnipresencia entre líneas de De Bruyne, a la vez que estiraba el campo por las bandas de Di Lorenzo y Politano. Un centro de éste lo remató Hojlund a la cruceta. Acto seguido, un grave error del propio Politano en una cesión defensiva permitió a Mikautadze empatar el partido tras superar de un disparo cruzado a un desconcertado Milinkovic-Savic fuera de su portería. El Nápoles trató de empujar al Villarreal contra su campo y lo que hizo fue invitarlo a explotar el contragolpe. Con el rival desordenado, Mouriño enganchó un derechazo desde fuera del área para remontar el encuentro en cuatro minutos. El Nápoles le dio una vuelta de tuerca al partido para apretarle las clavijas a un Villarreal que hacía tiempo que no se veía por delante en el marcador en la máxima competición continental. Al submarino le tocó cerrar espacios, pero sin renunciar a su estilo. Badiashile evitó un remate a bocajarro de Gerard en el área pequeña tras un jugadón de Moleiro. Aún tuvo tiempo Luiz Júnior, titular por fuerza mayor ante la baja de Gulacsi, de reivindicarse delante Hojlund. Y después llegó el golazo de Oluwseyi que permitió a La Cerámica disfrutar de los minutos finales de partido.

articles.title: United taught a lesson at highest level in 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid on sobering night
articles.summary: Manchester United kicked off against Atletico Madrid in their second match of the Champions League league phase.First halfMichael Carrick’s message before ki...
articles.body:
Manchester United kicked off against Atletico Madrid in their second match of the Champions League league phase.

Michael Carrick's message before kick-off would have been to keep it tight, but United did not take heed of the message.

After just a minute, the hosts had the lead. Álex Baena was onto a ball over the defence, got into the area and squared for Pablo Barrios, whose shot trickled into the back of the net.

United responded quite well, and Bryan Mbeumo got a shot off that bent just wide of the post in a decent retort. The visitors kept the ball for a while, and Mbeumo was once again through, but he poked his effort wide of the onrushing Jan Oblak.

On the half-hour mark, United came close again, but Mbeumo's shot after a quick one-two with Youri Tielemans was well stopped by the keeper. Carlos Baleba then had a glorious chance to open his account for the club, but he could only guide his free header right at Oblak.

United almost found themselves further behind shortly after, but Alejandro Grimaldo's free-kick rattled the post. The away side thought they had gone two down just before half-time, but Johnny Cardoso's strike was ruled out for a handball in the build-up by Marcos Llorente.

United came out looking to create chances, but it was the home side who once again went close. Julian Alvarez found space in the box, but his effort hit the inside of the post and trickled away from goal.

The away side had their clearest chance of the night when Youri Tielemans expertly picked out Bruno Fernandes in space, but he lifted the ball just over Oblak but wide of the goal. On the hour mark, Fernandes almost found Mbeumo in the box, but the ball was just cleared in time.

Shortly after, Alex Baena's fierce drive was well caught by Senne Lammens in goal. United responded, and Bruno Fernandes' effort was deflected into the hands of Oblak with 20 minutes left.

The Red Devils almost conjured something out of nothing when Fernandes took a short corner and curled the ball onto the crossbar with Oblak stranded.

The game took a massive twist when Leny Yoro was sent off for a foul as the last man on Jonathan David. After a VAR review, the young Frenchman was given his marching orders, and United were down to ten.

United wilted after just a few moments, and after David's shot was stopped by Lammens, Ademola Lookman pounced to put the result beyond doubt. Atletico proceeded to keep the ball and showed United the levels they need to reach to ever be considered potential winners of the competition again.

Llorente broke forward, but the ball was intercepted by Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez before a third could be added. The Red Devils almost got a consolation, but Matheus Cunha's effort was well stopped by Oblak.

The match petered out, and United have gone another game without a win as they crashed to their first defeat of the Champions League campaign.

articles.title: Four things we learned as Man United hit a new low after another damaging defeat in Madrid
articles.summary: Manchester United were back in action tonight, taking on Atlético Madrid at the Wanda Metropolitano.Winless in four matches and with pressure mounting on Mic...
articles.body:
Manchester United were back in action tonight, taking on Atlético Madrid at the Wanda Metropolitano.

Winless in four matches and with pressure mounting on Michael Carrick, this was the perfect chance for the Red Devils to prove their poor run was just a blip and silence the doubters.

Unfortunately, that was not the case, as the Red Devils left Madrid with another defeat. Atlético won 2-0 in a game United finished with 10 men, after the referee sent off Leny Yoro for denying Jonathan David a clear goalscoring opportunity.

This game had plenty to pick from. Here is what we picked:

United have kept just one clean sheet in nine games this season, and only two in their last 12 across all competitions. This cannot continue to be ignored. If they are to compete, they cannot keep going into matches expecting to concede.

They say if you cannot win, do not lose. The Red Devils must defend their goal properly, become hard to break down, and build from that foundation.

Bruno Fernandes at right wing was a tactical blunder

Bruno Fernandes started on the right but did not have the impact he should have had, as he lacks positional discipline. He drifted inwards constantly and left Dalot to fight for his life against Alejandro Grimaldo and Álex Baena.

Leaving Grimaldo free was unwise. He is one of Atlético's biggest threats, and the danger he posed made that clear. It is surprising Carrick and his assistants did not spot sooner that the left-back was so free, with so much space to do damage.

Fernandes must improve his positional discipline. If not, Carrick needs to be bold enough to drop him when things are not working.

Andrey Santos has rarely been given a clear chance to prove himself. He has played little since the 2-0 loss to Hull City. This rare start against Atlético Madrid, with Kobbie Mainoo injured, was his opportunity to press for a key role. He failed to take it. His performance was unconvincing.

Too often, the Brazilian misjudged his passes. The summer recruit impressed in pre-season but looked lost against Atlético and struggled to impose himself. This game did little to strengthen his case for a key role.

Carlos Baleba, by contrast, who just returned from injury, had a strong game. He did the basics well and showed the desire to win every ball. He is forcing his way into a key role and will be hard to ignore.

At times, the changes Carrick should make are obvious. He should have introduced Amad at the break to fill the hole on the right that Fernandes kept leaving. He should also have replaced Marcus Rashford with Matheus Cunha at half-time. Cunha would have helped United keep possession and influence the game, something Rashford was not doing.

Yet Carrick makes changes only when he wants to, and they rarely affect the game. His in-game decisions remain a concern.

That said, the United legend cannot seem to catch a break, and this defeat piles on the pressure. It is unlikely to cost him his job, yet it could be one of the results that shortens his time in the role.

Up next is the Roses derby, with United travelling to Leeds at Elland Road on Sunday afternoon.

Vitally, United need a big result against one of their fiercest rivals, or heads will roll.

articles.title: UCL | Villarreal 3-1 Napoli: Allegri’s men collapse in Champions League
articles.summary: Napoli fumbled a lead with Amir Rrahmani and fell apart for a 3-1 Champions League defeat to Villarreal, including a Matteo Politano howler of a back-pass.Th...
articles.body:
Napoli fumbled a lead with Amir Rrahmani and fell apart for a 3-1 Champions League defeat to Villarreal, including a Matteo Politano howler of a back-pass.

The Partenopei lost their opening Champions League fixture 1-0 at home to Arsenal , but were boosted by Saturday's 3-0 Serie A win over Frosinone. Scott McTominay had his first start five weeks on from heart surgery to correct a mild benign arrhythmia, but Frank Anguissa, Mathias Olivera, Antonio Vergara, Alisson Santos, Costantino Favasuli and Alessandro Buongiorno were out of action. Giovane was added to the UEFA list and thrown straight into the starting XI.

Villarreal lost 3-2 at Borussia Dortmund in Europe and sat 11 th in LaLiga going into this game, missing injured Nicolas Pepe and former Inter midfielder Tajon Buchanan. Goalkeeper Peter Gulacsi was expected to start, but withdrew from the squad after it was revealed his home was targeted in an armed robbery late last night with his family present.

Former Juventus defender Renato Veiga at full stretch prevented the Giovane roll across reaching Rasmus Hojlund, but the opener came soon after.

Kevin De Bruyne's short corner was floated to the back post by Billy Gilmour, where the Amir Rrahmani header was sensationally palmed onto the underside of the crossbar, but the Napoli defender was ready to turn in the rebound.

VILLARREAL, SPAIN – OCTOBER 13: Scott McTominay of SSC Napoli celebrates as teammate Amir Rrahmani (not pictured) scores his team's first goal during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between Villarreal CF and SSC Napoli at Estadio de la Ceramica on October 13, 2026 in Villarreal, Spain. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Villarreal fought back, as only a desperate Benoit Badiashile deflection stopped Georges Mikautadze drilling in the equaliser from just inside the area, then on the resulting corner Pape Gueye fired inches wide.

There was a frantic 60 seconds of action, as first Rasmus Hojlund saw his header on the Matteo Politano cross bounce off the frame of the goal.

Moments later, Politano's horrible back-pass was intercepted by Mikautadze, who drew Vanja Milinkovic-Savic out to score from the tightest of angles into the empty net.

VILLARREAL, SPAIN – OCTOBER 13: Georges Mikautadze of Villarreal CF scores his team's first goal during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between Villarreal CF and SSC Napoli at Estadio de la Ceramica on October 13, 2026 in Villarreal, Spain. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

The game turned on its head, as then Villarreal went in front with a screamer from distance by Santiago Mourino that flew past Milinkovic-Savic's fingertips.

It was end to end, with McTominay's free header flashing just wide, and dangerous counter-attacks from Mikautadze and Politano.

Luiz Junior was very alert after the restart to rush off his line and push the Billy Gilmour through ball off the feet of Hojlund, while Benoit Badiashile made a decisive interception to stop a tap-in from six yards.

Napoli struggled to break Villarreal down in the second half, then failed to make the most of a good situation when playing against nine men for a few minutes over the new delayed substitution rules.

VILLARREAL, SPAIN – OCTOBER 13: Santiago Mourino of Villarreal CF celebrates scoring his team's second goal with teammate Georges Mikautadze during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between Villarreal CF and SSC Napoli at Estadio de la Ceramica on October 13, 2026 in Villarreal, Spain. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

When Luiz Junior fumbled a free kick, Hojlund volleyed the rebound onto his own face, then on another move he dribbled past three only to make the angle too narrow.

De Bruyne's cross to the back post grazed both the head of Lorenzo Lucca and the studs of Di Lorenzo, but instead Villarreal added a third late on.

Nathan Saliba's pass found Ayoze Perez, a heavy first touch turned into an accidental assist for Tani Oluwaseyi to sweep in relatively undisturbed.

Rrahmani 8 (N), Mikautadze 23 (V), Mourino 26 (V), Oluwaseyi 86 (V)

articles.title: Dellenger: ESPN and CFP are ‘close’ to 24-team playoff deal, contrary to other reports
articles.summary: On Friday, College Football Playoff leadership, which comprises the 10 FBS conference commissioners plus Notre Dame AD Pete Bevacqua, sent a formal proposal...
articles.body:
On Friday, College Football Playoff leadership, which comprises the 10 FBS conference commissioners plus Notre Dame AD Pete Bevacqua, sent a formal proposal on a 24-team playoff to ESPN for review. ESPN now has five business days to respond to the proposal, and if no deal is reached, the CFP can bring rights to the expanded postseason to the open market, where other networks can bid on the inventory.

Several reports have characterized it as unlikely that ESPN and CFP leadership will reach a deal prior to the conclusion of the network's five-day consideration period, and a report in Sports Business Journal earlier this month described negotiations between the two sides as "tough sledding."

But one college football insider believes a deal is closer than reports are letting on.

On a recent episode of the College Football Enquirer podcast , Yahoo Sports college football reporter Ross Dellenger, who has been at the forefront of the playoff expansion story, suggested that ESPN and the CFP are quite close to a deal, although it's still quite possible the CFP tests the open market for due diligence purposes.

"There were some things that came out last week that sort of portrayed it that they're not close [to a deal], I think they're close. I think ESPN and the CFP are close on a deal," Dellenger said. "That doesn't mean the CFP is just going to agree to one, because why would you not go to the open market and just see what's out there?"

ESPN has a few built-in advantages when it comes to landing a deal for the expanded playoff. For one, they have this exclusive negotiating window with the CFP, and the two sides have been afforded time to hammer out intricacies of a 24-team playoff format that other networks have not gotten. Secondly, ESPN can put the money it currently allocates towards conference championship games, which will be eliminated in a 24-team playoff format, directly towards the cost of the expanded playoff. In total, reports estimate that ESPN allocates about $200 million per year for conference championship games, with much of that value being derived from the SEC and ACC title matchups.

"I think it's going to be really hard for any other network to get close to ESPN's offer because ESPN already has $200 million invested in the conference championship games, so they got kind of a head start," Dellenger explains.

And lastly, if CFP rights do hit the open market, ESPN has the opportunity to match any offer from a competing network should it get outbid.

Importantly, Dellenger notes that even if ESPN's five-day period expires and the two sides have not reached a deal, that does not mean CFP rights automatically go to the open market. The CFP and ESPN can, more or less, extend that period indefinitely if they're locked into negotiations, though Dellenger says there's an appetite by some in CFP leadership to test the open market just to see what offers an expanded playoff could attract. ESPN does, however, have a Dec. 1 deadline by which a deal would need to be done for expansion to be implemented next season.

Considering that one other prominent college football insider, The Athletic's Ralph Russo, expressed confidence that ESPN would be the sole home of a 24-team playoff , Dellenger's insistence that a deal is closer than other reports suggest isn't that crazy. Outside of Fox's initial push for 24 teams , which itself was partly a strategy to get rights onto the open market, there hasn't been a ton of interest from other networks about getting involved in CFP rights.

All signs seemingly point to ESPN as the frontrunner to keep all of the College Football Playoff. But how we get there is anyone's guess.

articles.title: Bayern Munich stunned by Viking FK in 3-3 Champions League draw
articles.summary: FC Bayern did not see this one coming.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich scuffled its way to a 3-3 Champions League league phase draw with Viking FK in a match that will not leave many fans feeling good about much.

For the second consecutive game, Bayern Munich put itself in an early hole. While not quite 8.4 seconds into the match like against FC Augsburg, Viking defender Gianni Stensness skied over Jonathan Tah and Kim Min-jae to get his head on the end of a corner from Zlatko Tripić to make it 1-0 in favor of the home side just over a minute into the match.

It was heavily referenced in pregame scouting reports that Bayern Munich needed to be wary of Viking's set pieces, but the Bavarians still somehow looked as if they were caught off-guard. It would not get much better for Bayern Munich, who—again—wasted several key scoring chances.

In the 38th minute, Peter Christiansen took advantage of a turnover by the Bavarians as he sprinted away from an unsuspecting Nathaniel Brown on a long run. Erik Botheim's long pass was perfectly weighted and found Christiansen in stride. Brown, who had no help from the team's center-backs on the play, had no angle to stop the Dane, who easily made it 2-0.

After an absolutely brutal first half, Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany had seen enough. The Belgian manager yanked Lennart Karl, Brown, and Tah off the pitch after a miserable performance, bringing on Ismael Saibari, Alphonso Davies, and Dayot Upamecano. Karl was a total non-factor, while his other ousted colleagues had big mistakes attached to them.

Bayern Munich would catch a break after Viking got a little too brazen with its fouls and brought down Konrad Laimer for a foul in the box. Harry Kane would put home the penalty attempt to make it 2-1 at the 54-minute mark.

That moment would give Bayern Munich the momentum it needed to mount a comeback.

Six minutes later, Joshua Kimmich sent in a cross that found Kane's head, and the Englishman made sure to put this attempt away as well to knot the game at 2-2. It looked like Luis Díaz instantly made it 3-2 after Kane's goal, but his bad-luck streak continued as he was whistled for an offside call.

Finally, in the 71st minute, Kane propelled Bayern Munich to its third goal. Kane lofted a perfect diagonal cross to a cutting Laimer, who pushed the ball to Díaz for a goal that the Colombian desperately needed.

Of course, Bayern Munich had to make things interesting as Michael Olise was sent off with a red card after picking up his second yellow card on a very selfish play, where he tossed the ball at Tripić and hit him in the face.

That would prove to be a death knell for Bayern Munich's hopes to retain the lead.

In the final minute of regulation, Bayern Munich was dispossessed twice (and maybe fouled) in their own end as Konrad Laimer and Kane both lost the ball, which led to Tripić hitting Herman Johan Haugen with a perfect cross. The right-back rose up over Davies and headed the ball in to tie the game at 3-3 in one of the most dramatic Champions League finishes in a very long time.

In the end, artificial turf did not matter. Bayern Munich's talent and depth did not matter. Only the fight and energy of a Viking side that will never forget this monumental night mattered.

articles.title: UCL | Inter 3-4 Club Brugge: Terrific Tresoldi hat-trick dooms Chivu
articles.summary: Nicolò Tresoldi made clear why Italy want him so much by scoring a hat-trick for Club Brugge’s shock 4-3 victory, but Inter are on zero points after two Cham...
articles.body:
Nicolò Tresoldi made clear why Italy want him so much by scoring a hat-trick for Club Brugge's shock 4-3 victory, but Inter are on zero points after two Champions League games.

The Nerazzurri paid a heavy price for individual errors in the 2-1 defeat to Real Madrid , so needed to be on their toes. Curtis Jones and John Stones were out injured, while Aleksandar Stankovic was again benched against the club where he won the Belgian title last season.

Club Brugge lost 3-2 to Aston Villa and saw Yann Sommer face his former team, along with potential Italy international hitman Nicolò Tresoldi, but Joel Ordonez missed out with a fractured metatarsal.

MILAN, ITALY – OCTOBER 13: Andy Diouf of FC Internazionale Milano has his shot saved by Yann Sommer of Club Brugge KV during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between FC Internazionale Milano and Club Brugge KV at Stadio San Siro on October 13, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Sommer rushed off his line to deny Andy Diouf at the near post, then could only watch as the Marcus Thuram angled drive flashed across the face of goal to skim the back post.

Another Diouf pull-back from the by-line saw Brandon Mechele charge down the Lautaro Martinez tap-in, but Tresoldi was unlucky not to put the Belgians in front from a corner when he smashed his finish against the crossbar.

Inter were made to pay for an excess of enthusiasm when Club Brugge broke from a corner with Carlos Forbs sprinting from his own box to the other penalty area, where he was brought down by Hakan Calhanoglu. Tresoldi converted the resulting penalty into the roof of the net, a special moment for the Italo-German lifelong Milan fan.

MILAN, ITALY – OCTOBER 13: Nicolo Tresoldi of Club Brugge KV scores his team's first goal from the penalty spot during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between FC Internazionale Milano and Club Brugge KV at Stadio San Siro on October 13, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Calhanoglu tried to make up for his error straight away, but fired one of his trademark efforts onto the crossbar.

Lautaro Martinez had the ball in the net on 36 minutes from a free kick, but was offside for the free header.

Jorne Spileers made a decisive block on Lautaro Martinez after Kyriani Sabbe was sold a dummy, and Bastoni's header was smothered by Sommer on the resulting corner.

Lautaro Martinez did get the equaliser soon after, as Marcus Thuram surged down the left and laid it off for the Dimarco back-heel flick, where the Inter captain sold another dummy to turn a defender and sweep in from six yards. It was his first Champions League goal since November 2025.

MILAN, ITALY – OCTOBER 13: Lautaro Martinez of FC Internazionale Milano scores his team's first goal during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between FC Internazionale Milano and Club Brugge KV at Stadio San Siro on October 13, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Thuram fired over from the edge of the area, but Mechele suffered a very painful albeit entirely unintentional nose injury after a collision with Diouf.

Lautaro Martinez went clear on goal only to be denied by a desperate Sommer outstretched boot, then the follow-up was blocked by defenders.

Spileers had to be carried off injured after his brave sliding tackle on Dimarco, but Club Brugge restored their advantage as Inter were once again made to pay for individual errors.

Dimarco could not keep up with the pace of Forbs and Josep Martinez was caught in no man's land, allowing Tresoldi to deposit into an empty net.

Club Brugge almost added another, as Virgili swung first-time from 12 yards to bounce off the inside of the near post, then Josep Martinez had to make a big save on Potts one-on-one.

MILAN, ITALY – OCTOBER 13: Nicolo Tresoldi of Club Brugge KV celebrates scoring his team's second goal during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between FC Internazionale Milano and Club Brugge KV at Stadio San Siro on October 13, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Tresoldi completed his dream hat-trick when pouncing on the rebound from another Josep Martinez save on the sprightly Forbs.

Inter have come back from 2-0 down to win several Serie A games this season and therefore felt belief when Sommer parried a Petar Sucic screamer into the path of Lautaro Martinez for 3-2.

However, Club Brugge added a fourth instead when Djed Spence's wayward pass was intercepted by Forbs, who sent Romeo Vermant down the right to dink the finish over Josep Martinez.

It still wasn't over, as Potts slipped on the Aleksandar Stankovic through ball, allowing Ange-Yoan Bonny to get down the left, cut inside and curl a right-foot finish into the far top corner, but that was scant consolation.

Tresoldi pen 30, 63, 74 (B), Lautaro Martinez 44, 81 (I), Vermant 87 (B), Bonny 93 (I)

articles.title: Alessandro Canovi says Juventus is doing its best with the current squad
articles.summary: Juventus have endured a difficult start to the season, leaving Luciano Spalletti with the task of getting the club back on track. Expectations remain high, d...
articles.body:
Juventus have endured a difficult start to the season, leaving Luciano Spalletti with the task of getting the club back on track. Expectations remain high, despite performances falling short of supporters' hopes.

Spalletti has experience of winning the Scudetto, having achieved that with Napoli three years ago. Juventus will hope he can bring the title back to Turin, although that ambition may require time and progress.

Juve are not widely regarded as genuine title contenders this season. Supporters expect a great deal from the black and white side, but the team have struggled for consistency. There is still time to improve in the league and collect results in Europe, yet winning the Scudetto or Europa League looks difficult.

Juventus continue to search for consistency

The team's unpredictability has made it difficult to assess their prospects. It can be hard to know which version of Juventus will appear before kick off. More reliable performances are needed if they are to challenge the leading sides.

Alessandro Canovi has been following Juventus and believes they are doing as much as possible with the players available. Speaking via Tuttomercatoweb , he argued that the pressure surrounding the club should not be seen as a problem for the coach alone.

"It's a world that asks a lot of you. I don't think it's just a coaching thing, it's all a whole. In my opinion, Juventus is getting the most out of this squad."

(Photo by Alessandro Sabattini/Getty Images)

Canovi's comments suggest Spalletti should not carry all the responsibility for Juventus' difficulties. Managing the club brings significant expectations, while results also depend on the squad's quality and balance. Canovi believes the team are getting a great deal from their current players.

Juventus still have time to improve this season, but they need stronger performances and more regular results. Greater consistency would help them compete for major honours.

Spalletti's success at Napoli gives Juventus reason to believe he can build towards future silverware. For now, Canovi believes the team are making the most of their resources, despite performances that have not met the club's expectations.

articles.title: Bristol City 0-1 Blackburn: Rovers goalkeeper Balazs Toth stars as Tony Mowbray's side secure hard-fought win at Ashton Gate
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Bristol City and Blackburn at Ashton Gate on Tuesday; Oladapo Afolayan's goal sealed a narrow win for Rovers on a night where goalkeeper Balazs Toth starred
articles.body:
The visitors had Toth to thank for still being in the game when Oladapo Afolayan rifled them into a 38th-minute lead with a clean right-footed shot from the corner of the box which wrong-footed motionless home goalkeeper Sam Tickle.

Toth was simply unbeatable on the night, making a string of outstanding saves, particularly in the first half. His efforts left City with nothing to show from a performance that started impressively and ended in massive frustration.

Robins boss Michael Skubala rotated his squad, making five changes from the 1-1 draw at Charlton, while Rovers manager Tony Mowbray recalled Tom Atcheson to the starting line-up in his only change from the 2-1 win over Cardiff.

The home side dominated the opening half hour and might well have been three or four up before falling behind. Dom Ballard alone could have had a hat-trick, but for the brilliance of Toth.

City's frontman got behind Blackburn's backline after 11 minutes, but delayed his shot and saw his low effort saved. That was nothing compared with Toth's superb save four minutes later, stretching every sinew to get a left hand to Ballard's well-placed header.

The busy striker went clear again in the 23rd minute, however, tried to make too sure of scoring and had his shot blocked to safety. Two minutes later, Toth flung himself to his left to keep out George Tanner's header from a Jed Wallace cross.

A Bristol City goal looked inevitable, though, Rovers weathered the storm and, while Afolayan's strike came out of the blue, they had more of the game as half-time approached.

Skubala introduced winger Yu Hirakawa as a substitute for Sam Greenwood at the start of the second half and Toth was in action again, diving full length to keep out Scott Twine's 30-yard free-kick.

Next it was Hirawaka to be denied by the outstanding Rovers goalkeeper, who spread himself to keep out a low 54th-minute shot.

When City finally found a way past him after 75 minutes, Jed Wallace was ruled offside to increase their anxiety.

Both teams made numerous changes and City failed to repeat their first-half dominance.

Toth saved again from substitutes Tommy Horvat and Elijah Adebayo in the closing stages to complete a faultless contribution.

Adebayo headed over in stoppage time, but Rovers defended tenaciously and by then home fans had accepted it was not their team's night.

articles.title: Arsenal 3-0 Lille: Jurrien Timber, Eberechi Eze and Bukayo Saka on target as Gunners win in Champions League
articles.summary: Arsenal score three quick-fire goals to beat Lille 3-0 in the league phase of the Champions League; Jurrien Timber and Eberechi Eze scored their first goals of the season; Bukayo Saka was also on target six minutes after coming off the bench
articles.body:
The Gunners were frustrated for an hour at the Emirates Stadium but Jurrien Timber's superb finish, lifted over the goalkeeper from Noni Madueke's pass, opened the floodgates.

Eberechi Eze added the second with the help of a slight deflection from substitute Bukayo Saka's pass, and Saka added the third himself after slick interplay with Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, who were introduced alongside him after the opening goal.

Mikel Arteta used the visit of Lille to rotate his side, making five changes from the 2-1 win over Leeds as Arsenal begin a run of eight games in 25 days, but their substitutes helped to ensure they followed up last month's win over Napoli with another victory.

The Gunners should have led earlier with Bruno Guimaraes, starting for the first time at the Emirates Stadium as an Arsenal player, and Eze missing their best chances of the first period.

But Lille's resistance broken with Timber's opener and Davide Ancelotti's side couldn't contain the Gunners, whose substitutions underlined their strength in depth, with Saka particularly impressive before another eye-catching cameo from Max Dowman.

At the other end, Lille did not register a shot on target, although striker Olivier Giroud received a positive reception on his return to the Emirates Stadium as a substitute.

The victory continues a positive start to Arsenal's Champions League campaign as last year's runners-up aim to go one better.

Ancelotti: We couldn't match their rhythm

"It's really tough. With the players they always have on the bench, they can change the rhythm of the game.

"For us it was difficult to keep up with the rhythm they put after 60 minutes.

"We have to keep the good things we did for 55 or 60 minutes.

"To come here and get a good result, you have to have many things aligned and we didn't have that.

"It's too hard on the players, the score. They didn't deserve this score."

articles.title: Atletico Madrid 2-0 Man Utd: Leny Yoro sent off in Champions League as Michael Carrick's side extend winless run to five games
articles.summary: Man Utd conceded after 47 seconds vs Atletico Madrid after being cut open with a simple ball over the top and the hosts added a second late in the game shortly after Leny Yoro was shown a straight red card following an on-field review by referee Glenn Nyberg
articles.body:
United, now winless in five games in all competitions, went behind after just 47 seconds as Atletico sliced through with a simple ball over the top which allowed Alex Baena to square for Pablo Barrios to give Carrick a nightmare start in Madrid.

Substitute Ademola Lookman sealed the victory for Diego Simeone's side late in the second half with Atletico's second goal just five minutes after Yoro was shown a straight red card following an on-field review by referee Glenn Nyberg.

The France international was deemed to have denied Atletico's Jonathan David a goalscoring opportunity after a coming together between the pair just inside United's half. "It is soft! No way, that should not be a red," Clinton Morrison said on Soccer Special.

The referee had earlier disallowed Johnny Cardoso's goal for Atletico just before half-time that would have doubled their lead, with Marcos Llorente judged to have handled the ball when his arm was in an unnatural position in the build up.

United were clearly second best but had more than enough opportunities to draw level with Bryan Mbeumo sending a deflected shot narrowly wide and captain Bruno Fernandes hitting the bar after spurning a decent opening on the break.

United, who remain on three points in the Champions League league phase, can have no complaints about losing in Madrid after yet another disjointed performance which only adds to the scrutiny on their head coach ahead of a Sunday's trip to Leeds in the league, live on Sky Sports .
